Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.

ru.title: Красивая картинка — ещё не согласованный 3D-мир
ru.desc: Orbia — это новый бенчмарк для систематической оценки 3D-согласованности интерактивных video world models, то есть генеративных моделей видео, которые работают как виртуальные миры. Авторы оценивают три аспекта: сохранение входного изображения, устойчивость сгенерированного контента при повторном обращении к областям и внутреннюю 3D-согласованность между видами, включая соответствие глубины, признаков и масштаба. Для построения бенчмарка использовались публичные датасеты, собственные съёмки и симуляции, что дало 720 примеров в помещениях и на улице с шестью протоколами исследования и возвратов. Оценка охватывает 27 моделей, управляемых текстом, действиями или положением камеры, и показывает, что реалистичная картинка не гарантирует согласованный 3D-мир.

en.title: Ensuring 3D Consistency in Interactive Video Worlds
en.desc: Orbia is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the 3D consistency of interactive video world models. It focuses on three key dimensions: input preservation, content persistence, and geometric self-consistency, ensuring that generated worlds maintain their structure and appearance over time. The benchmark uses controlled exploration and revisit protocols to assess how well models retain and reproduce 3D scenes. By analyzing various models through this systematic approach, Orbia aims to improve the reliability of interactive video simulations.

zh.title: Orbia：评估交互式视频世界模型的3D一致性
zh.desc: Orbia是一个基准测试，旨在系统地评估交互式视频世界模型中的3D一致性。它通过控制探索、重访协议和多维度测量来实现，包括输入保留、内容持久性和几何自一致性。该基准测试使用RGB-D参考和注释锚点来支持外观、几何和空间稳定性测量。Orbia为诊断3D不一致性和开发更持久的视频世界模型提供了系统基础。

papers.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract Researchers propose a four-level hierarchy for multimodal generative models and introduce the WorldCast benchmark to evaluate multi-step world state prediction, revealing rapid progress by frontier systems but substantial gaps in open-source models for reasoning-heavy visual forecasting.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Humans interpret multimodal observations of the world and forecast how it will evolve. Recent multimodal generative systems have demonstrated similar capabilities: they can integrate multimodal context and synthesize visual outputs that depict changes in the world. To characterize this emerging trajectory, we organize model capabilities into a four-level hierarchy and discover that higher-level tasks remain relatively underexplored despite model progress. To bridge this gap, we explore model performance on multi-step world state prediction, a high-level task that requires models to forecast successive future world states from multimodal observations and diverse references. Such a task requires models to possess entangled understanding and generation capabilities, as well as extensive world knowledge to translate human action sequences, physical transformations, and abstract visual reasoning into coherent visual outputs. We introduce WorldCast, a benchmark comprising 320 manually designed cases across eight categories, and evaluate 12 representative models. The conducted experiments yield three key insights: (a) advances in frontier models are rapidly pushing the boundaries of intelligent world modeling, with the GPT-Image-2.5 System scoring 72.8 and demonstrating early-stage visual state prediction capabilities on real-world tasks; (b) WorldCast reveals substantial gaps between models: even Nano Banana Pro reaches only 42.8 and the best open-source model scores 20.1, with deficits in handling complex context, entangled references, and reasoning-heavy tasks; (c) strong generative models effectively draw on the capabilities of their underlying language models. These findings highlight the need for multimodal generative models that are capable of dynamic planning and reasoning while also being deeply unified to faithfully simulate real-world states.

ru.title: Предсказать будущее мира по картинкам: пока только закрытые модели умеют это хорошо
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают четырёхуровневую иерархию возможностей мультимодальных генеративных моделей и показывают, что задачи верхних уровней изучены слабо. Для их проверки введён бенчмарк WorldCast из 320 вручную составленных кейсов, где модель должна предсказать последовательность будущих состояний мира по мультимодальным наблюдениям. Эксперименты на 12 моделях показывают, что лучшая закрытая система GPT-Image-2.5 набирает 72.8 балла, тогда как лучшая открытая модель только 20.1, особенно слабо модели справляются со сложным контекстом и рассуждениями. Результаты также подтверждают, что сильная генерация опирается на возможности базовой LLM, поэтому нужны модели, которые объединяют планирование, рассуждение и моделирование реального мира.

en.title: Bridging Gaps in Multimodal World State Prediction
en.desc: This paper introduces a four-level hierarchy for multimodal generative models, which are systems that can understand and create outputs based on different types of data, like images and text. The authors present the WorldCast benchmark to assess how well these models can predict future states of the world based on multimodal observations. Their research shows that while advanced models are making progress, there are still significant gaps in performance, especially in tasks that require complex reasoning and understanding. The findings emphasize the importance of developing models that can integrate knowledge and reasoning to accurately simulate real-world scenarios.

zh.title: 多模态生成模型的未来挑战与机遇
zh.desc: 研究人员提出了一个四级层次结构，用于多模态生成模型，并引入了WorldCast基准来评估多步世界状态预测。尽管前沿系统在智能世界建模方面取得了快速进展，但开源模型在需要推理的视觉预测任务中仍存在显著差距。通过对320个手动设计案例的评估，发现高层次任务仍然相对未被充分探索，尤其是在处理复杂上下文和抽象视觉推理方面。研究结果强调了需要能够进行动态规划和推理的多模态生成模型，以真实地模拟现实世界状态。

papers.title: InfoVis: Unified Slide Image Generation and Editing
papers.abstract: Abstract InfoVis is a unified 9B model for slide generation and editing trained on millions of native records and evaluated on a new multidimensional benchmark, achieving top open-source performance across text rendering, instruction following, visual grounding, design, and editing.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generating and editing presentation slides requires models to combine accurate text rendering, instruction following, visual grounding, aesthetic design, and precise editing within one canvas. Existing work covers only subsets of these capabilities and lacks large-scale slide-native supervision and diagnostic evaluation. We formulate four slide-centric tasks and build a scalable data engine with over 13M continual-pretraining records and 1.9M supervised fine-tuning records. We also introduce VisSlideBench, a benchmark of 1,527 manually screened instances that covers all four tasks with task-specific, multidimensional evaluation. Its automatic rankings agree with blinded, dimension-wise human rankings. Using these resources, we train InfoVis, a unified 9B slide generation and editing model. On VisSlideBench, InfoVis leads every evaluated open-source model on all eleven metrics and scores 7.94 overall against 7.99 for Nano-Banana-2. Starting from FLUX.2-klein-base-9B, slide-specific post-training adds 1.6 points overall, with the largest generation gains in content faithfulness; the remaining gap to proprietary models is smallest in content faithfulness and largest in aesthetic quality. Built on InfoVis, our document-to-slide workflow achieves the second-highest Aesthetics score on the external SlidesGen-Bench. We will release the model, code, data, and benchmark.
affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
University of Science and Technology of China

ru.title: Одна модель для создания и редактирования слайдов с открытым исходным кодом
ru.desc: Статья представляет InfoVis — унифицированную модель на 9B параметров для генерации и редактирования слайдов, обученную на более чем 13 млн записей для continual pretraining и 1,9 млн для supervised fine-tuning. Авторы также создали бенчмарк VisSlideBench из 1527 вручную отобранных примеров с многомерной оценкой по четырём задачам. На этом бенчмарке InfoVis опережает все открытые модели по всем одиннадцати метрикам и почти догоняет проприетарную модель Nano-Banana-2 (7.94 против 7.99). Слабее всего модель выглядит в эстетике дизайна, а ближе всего к проприетарным решениям — в точности содержания.

en.title: Revolutionizing Slide Generation with InfoVis
en.desc: The paper presents InfoVis, a comprehensive model designed for generating and editing presentation slides by integrating multiple machine learning capabilities such as text rendering, instruction following, visual grounding, and design aesthetics. It addresses the limitations of existing models that only tackle subsets of these tasks by utilizing a large dataset of over 13 million records for continual pretraining and 1.9 million for supervised fine-tuning. The authors introduce VisSlideBench, a new benchmark for evaluating slide generation tasks, which includes 1,527 instances and provides multidimensional assessments that align with human evaluations. InfoVis outperforms all other open-source models on this benchmark, demonstrating significant improvements in content accuracy and overall performance, while also highlighting areas for further enhancement in aesthetic quality.

zh.title: 统一幻灯片生成与编辑的强大模型
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为InfoVis的统一9B模型，用于生成和编辑幻灯片。该模型经过数百万条原生记录的训练，并在新的多维基准上进行了评估，展现出卓越的开源性能。InfoVis结合了文本渲染、指令跟随、视觉定位、美学设计和精确编辑等多种能力，填补了现有研究的空白。我们还构建了VisSlideBench基准，涵盖了四个幻灯片中心任务，并提供了全面的评估指标。

papers.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch
papers.abstract: Abstract A multi-agent engine synthesizes data environments and tasks to train models for analytical insight discovery, improving performance across benchmarks without trajectory distillation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Data agents use code to process heterogeneous files and derive analytical insights. Scaling their training faces costly environment curation, privacy and intellectual-property restrictions, and difficulty verifying open-ended findings without known generative truth. Our core insight is to specify the world behind the files before generating the files themselves. We introduce Data World, a multi-agent engine that synthesizes environments, tasks, and rubrics from explicit mechanisms. Independent audits check target recoverability from observed files; rubrics support evaluation and RL rewards. Human preference-based curation for question realism selects 100 tasks across 50 held-out worlds and 16 domains for DataWorld-Bench. The engine also yields 2,135 training tasks from 1,037 disjoint worlds. Evaluation of ten frontier models shows that the benchmark remains challenging, particularly for insight discovery, with a consistent computation-insight gap. RL-zero training on the synthesized tasks produces DataWorld-35B-A3B from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B without trajectory distillation. Under matched evaluation, it improves over its base by 7.06 points on DataWorld-Bench, 14.28 on DAComp, 20.90 on DABstep-Hard, and 12.13 on JobBench, a broader occupational benchmark.
affiliations: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

ru.title: Сначала мир, потом данные: обучение аналитических агентов без дорогой разметки
ru.desc: Авторы представляют Data World — мультиагентный движок, который синтезирует среды данных, задачи и рубрики, исходя из явно заданных механизмов мира, а не наоборот. Независимые аудиты проверяют, можно ли восстановить целевые величины по наблюдаемым файлам, а рубрики используются для оценки и как reward в RL. На основе движка создан DataWorld-Bench (100 задач из 50 отложенных миров) и 2135 обучающих задач, а модель DataWorld-35B-A3B обучена с помощью RL-zero без дистилляции траекторий. Модель превосходит базовую Qwen3.6-35B-A3B на 7–21 пункт на нескольких бенчмарках, при этом инсайт-анализ остаётся самым сложным этапом.

en.title: Revolutionizing Insight Discovery with Data World
en.desc: This paper presents a multi-agent engine called Data World that creates synthetic data environments and tasks to enhance model training for analytical insights. By specifying the underlying mechanisms of data generation, it addresses challenges like environment curation costs and privacy issues. The engine generates a diverse set of training tasks and employs independent audits to ensure the reliability of insights derived from the data. The results show significant performance improvements across various benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in reducing the computation-insight gap.

zh.title: 多智能体引擎提升分析洞察发现能力
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种多智能体引擎，能够合成数据环境和任务，以训练模型发现分析洞察。该引擎通过明确机制生成环境、任务和评估标准，避免了传统方法中的轨迹蒸馏问题。研究还提出了数据世界（Data World），通过独立审计确保从观察文件中恢复目标，并利用人类偏好进行任务选择。最终，实验结果显示，该引擎在多个基准测试中显著提高了模型的性能，尤其是在洞察发现方面。

papers.title: EdgeWise: Bringing Long-Horizon Agents to the Edge via Selective Cloud Delegation
papers.abstract: Abstract EdgeWise uses a local small language model with selective cloud delegation via reinforcement learning to reduce inference costs on long-horizon agent tasks without sacrificing performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Complex and long-horizon agent tasks often rely on frontier models deployed in the cloud to achieve strong performance. However, using these models for every step of a long-horizon trajectory incurs substantial inference cost, even though not all steps may require the same level of model capability. In this paper, we find that allocating the LLM to only a small subset of key steps can achieve performance comparable to full LLM execution while significantly reducing inference cost. Motivated by this observation, we propose EdgeWise, an edge-cloud collaboration framework that deploys an SLM on the local device as the primary solver and selectively delegates critical steps to a cloud LLM when stronger model capacity is needed. To enable autonomous delegation without additional models at inference time, we introduce a step-level RL method that jointly optimizes task solving and delegation, with fine-grained credit assignment for individual delegation decisions. We also introduce an external judge-based delegation strategy and use it to systematically investigate key design choices in edge-cloud collaboration, including when to delegate, how delegation decisions should be made, what context should be shared, and how frequently the cloud LLM should be invoked. Experiments show that EdgeWise matches or outperforms pure-LLM execution while reducing inference cost up to 62% on SWE-Rebench and 34% on Terminal-Bench 2.1. We further deploy EdgeWise on a local workstation, demonstrating comparable cost savings in a practical edge-cloud setting.

ru.title: Большая модель нужна лишь на ключевых шагах: экономим инференс без потери качества
ru.desc: Статья представляет EdgeWise — фреймворк совместной работы edge и cloud, где локальная SLM (small language model) решает задачу, а сложные шаги делегирует облачной LLM. Авторы показывают, что вызов большой LLM лишь на небольшом подмножестве ключевых шагов даёт качество, сравнимое с полным выполнением, при значительном снижении стоимости инференса. Делегирование обучается через step-level RL с тонкой credit assignment для каждого решения, без дополнительных моделей на этапе инференса. Эксперименты на SWE-Rebench и Terminal-Bench 2.1 показывают экономию до 62% и 34% соответственно при сохранении или улучшении качества.

en.title: Smart Delegation for Cost-Effective AI Tasks
en.desc: EdgeWise is a framework that combines local small language models (SLMs) with cloud-based large language models (LLMs) to optimize inference costs for long-horizon tasks. By using reinforcement learning, it selectively delegates only critical steps of a task to the cloud, allowing for significant cost savings without losing performance. The framework intelligently decides when and how to delegate tasks based on the complexity of each step, ensuring efficient use of resources. Experiments show that EdgeWise can reduce inference costs by up to 62% while maintaining performance comparable to using only LLMs.

zh.title: 边缘云协作，降低推理成本！
zh.desc: EdgeWise 是一种边缘云协作框架，旨在通过强化学习减少长时间任务的推理成本，同时保持性能。它使用本地的小型语言模型作为主要求解器，并在关键步骤上选择性地将任务委托给云端的大型语言模型。通过这种方式，EdgeWise 能够在不需要每一步都使用强大模型的情况下，显著降低推理成本。实验结果表明，EdgeWise 在多个基准测试中表现出色，推理成本降低高达62%。

papers.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract A post-training framework using hierarchical supervised fine-tuning and windowed interaction reinforcement learning trains a 35B mixture-of-experts agent to autonomously optimize long-horizon machine learning engineering workflows.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.

ru.title: Агент, который сам улучшает ML-эксперименты: длинные цепочки решений под контролем награды
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают метод пост-обучения (post-training) для автономной оптимизации длинных ML-инженерных процессов и обучают на его основе MLExpert, агентную модель Mixture-of-Experts на 35B параметров. Модель сначала проходит иерархический агентный SFT, который переносит навыки использования инструментов и программирования на задачи MLE, а затем обучается с помощью Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL), где несколько решений между последовательными результатами экспериментов получают общую награду по итоговому исходу. На MLE-Bench Lite средняя доля медалей выросла с 37,9% до 72,7%, что сопоставимо с более крупными frontier-моделями. Эксперименты на NatureBench Lite, оптимизации агентных каркасов и алгоритмов показывают, что обученная способность к оптимизации обобщается на другие задачи.

en.title: Autonomous Optimization for Machine Learning Workflows
en.desc: This paper presents a new framework for optimizing machine learning engineering workflows using a 35B mixture-of-experts model called MLExpert. It employs hierarchical supervised fine-tuning and windowed interaction reinforcement learning to enhance the model's ability to autonomously manage long-term experiments. The approach focuses on learning from feedback across multiple experiments, allowing the model to adapt its strategies based on previous outcomes. The results demonstrate significant improvements in performance metrics, indicating that the model can effectively generalize its optimization capabilities to various tasks.

zh.title: 自主优化机器学习工程的未来
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种后训练框架，利用分层监督微调和窗口交互强化学习，训练一个35B的混合专家模型，旨在自主优化长期的机器学习工程工作流。大型语言模型（LLMs）正在从辅助科学研究和工程转向自主开发和改进人工智能系统，推动人工智能自我改进的进程。通过复杂的协调，工作流驱动的机器学习工程系统为这一目标提供了实际路径，允许模型自主组织实验并根据执行反馈调整优化策略。实验结果表明，MLExpert在多个基准测试中显著提高了性能，展示了其优化能力的广泛适用性。

papers.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract Intern-Decision introduces compact multimodal models that output structured choices with probabilities via masked language modeling, achieving high accuracy and low latency for interactive agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Interactive agents repeatedly choose among a finite set of actions, labels, or ordinal outcomes. Generating a free-form response for each choice adds latency and complicates the interface between a model and its environment. We present Intern-Decision, a family of 0.8B, 2B, and 4B multimodal decision models that return structured choices and candidate probabilities from text and optional images. Our autoregressive masked language modeling objective places one decision placeholder per field in a complete assistant JSON skeleton. Ground-truth symbols appear only in supervision, while all fields are evaluated in a single causal forward pass using the backbone's native language-model head. The 4B model achieves a 90.02% unweighted average accuracy across seven evaluation suites, compared with 88.74% for Jev v1.13.0. For a fixed 289-token request with three fields on one RTX 4090, mean latency is 44.16 ms for the 4B model and approximately 33--34 ms for the smaller models. On a separate 96-case known-distribution pilot, temperature scaling reduces expected multiclass Brier from 0.628 to 0.550 and expected calibration error from 0.213 to 0.089. A confidence-based handoff study on 111 public Jevbench-Hard items improves accuracy from 82/111 (73.87%) to 97/111 (87.39%) by routing 42 items to Atria-Dawn-Preview. We also describe qualitative game, visual interface, and browser demonstrations. These results support compact decision models as a practical component of larger agent systems.

ru.title: Быстрые и откалиброванные решения вместо болтовни LLM
ru.desc: В статье представлено семейство компактных мультимодальных моделей Intern-Decision (0.8B, 2B и 4B), которые возвращают структурированный выбор и вероятности кандидатов по тексту и изображениям. Ключевая идея — авторегрессивное masked language modeling: для каждого поля JSON-шаблона ставится плейсхолдер, а все поля оцениваются за один causal forward pass через штатную языковую голову модели. Это позволяет избежать генерации свободного текста и заметно снижает задержку (около 44 мс для 4B на RTX 4090). Модели показывают высокую точность, улучшенную калибровку после temperature scaling и полезны как компонент больших агентных систем.

en.title: Efficient Decision-Making for Interactive Agents
en.desc: The paper presents Intern-Decision, a series of compact multimodal models designed for interactive agents that make structured choices with associated probabilities. By utilizing masked language modeling, these models can efficiently generate decisions without the need for lengthy free-form responses, thus reducing latency. The models, ranging from 0.8B to 4B parameters, demonstrate high accuracy, achieving a 90.02% average across various evaluation suites. Additionally, techniques like temperature scaling and confidence-based handoff improve the models' performance, making them suitable for integration into larger agent systems.

zh.title: 紧凑多模态决策模型的高效选择
zh.desc: Intern-Decision提出了一种紧凑的多模态模型，通过掩蔽语言建模输出结构化选择和概率，适用于交互式智能体。这些模型能够在有限的动作、标签或顺序结果中进行选择，减少了生成自由形式响应所带来的延迟。该模型系列包括0.8B、2B和4B参数的版本，能够从文本和可选图像中返回结构化选择和候选概率。实验结果显示，4B模型在多个评估套件中达到了90.02%的准确率，且在固定请求下的平均延迟为44.16毫秒，表现出色。

papers.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
papers.abstract: Abstract Terminal-RSI alternates recursive trajectory rewriting with critic-inheriting policy refinement to advance terminal agents from partial progress to strict verification.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Converting verifier outcomes into useful policy updates and partial progress into complete task resolution is crucial for terminal agents. We present Terminal-RSI, which alternates Recursive Self-Rewrite (RSR) of verified trajectories with critic-inheriting Recursive Policy-Refine (RPR). We formulate Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE (TB-GAE) to retain token-specific baselines while applying decay across interaction turns. Family Dense Reward (FDR) calibrates semantic progress across task families; Success-Prioritized Reward (SPR) separates strict success from bounded partial credit. A Warm-up Critic Model, recursive critic handoff, and stage-specific learning rates coordinate the two refinement phases. The five-stage sequence from Qwen3.8-27B base model through RSR-1, RPR-1, RSR-2, and RPR-2 yields Terminal-RSI-27B: 19.84% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 86.52% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 16.95% on Terminal-Bench 3.0, and 79.00% on Terminal-Bench Hard. On LHTB, process reward rises from 0.21 to 0.37 and strict completion from 0/46 to 5/46; SWR100 success doubles from 3.00% to 6.00%. By recursively coupling verified trajectory rewriting with critic-inheriting policy refinement, each retained stage consolidates discovered behaviors and progressively advances the agent from partial local repairs to strict terminal verification.

ru.title: От частичного прогресса к строгому успеху терминального агента через рекурсивное самопереписывание
ru.desc: В статье представлен Terminal-RSI — метод обучения терминальных LLM-агентов, который чередует рекурсивное переписывание верифицированных траекторий (RSR) и уточнение политики с наследованием критика (RPR). Для стабилизации обучения используются TB-GAE с учётом границ ходов, функция вознаграждения FDR для калибровки семантического прогресса и SPR, разделяющая строгий успех и частичный кредит. Пятиэтапная последовательность обучения на базе Qwen3.8-27B даёт модель Terminal-RSI-27B, которая показывает заметный рост результатов на бенчмарках Terminal-Bench и LHTB. Авторы заключают, что такое рекурсивное объединение переписывания траекторий и уточнения политики постепенно переводит агента от частичных локальных исправлений к строгой верификации выполнения задач.

en.title: Advancing Terminal Agents through Recursive Refinement
en.desc: The paper introduces Terminal-RSI, a method that enhances terminal agents' performance by combining recursive trajectory rewriting with policy refinement. It focuses on converting verification outcomes into actionable policy updates, allowing agents to progress from incomplete tasks to full resolution. The approach utilizes techniques like Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE for maintaining token-specific baselines and Family Dense Reward for measuring semantic progress. By systematically refining policies through multiple stages, Terminal-RSI significantly improves task completion rates across various benchmarks.

zh.title: 递归优化，助力智能体严格验证
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为Terminal-RSI的方法，通过递归轨迹重写和批评继承策略优化，帮助终端智能体从部分进展达到严格验证。该方法结合了验证轨迹的递归自重写（RSR）和批评继承的递归策略优化（RPR），以实现任务的完整解决。我们还引入了Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE（TB-GAE）和家庭密集奖励（FDR）等新概念，以提高智能体在不同任务中的表现。实验结果显示，Terminal-RSI在多个基准测试中显著提高了智能体的成功率和任务完成度。

papers.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract A graded visual verifier decomposes complex multimodal rules into pointwise scores and uses decoupled reinforcement learning to improve generalization, with pairwise verification further enhancing structured world-modeling accuracy.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.

ru.title: Оценивать по частям, а не просто да или нет: ключ к надёжным визуальным верификаторам
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают генеративный визуальный верификатор, который разбивает сложные мультимодальные промпты и правила на мелкие компоненты и выставляет каждому поточечную оценку вместо бинарного True/False. Для обучения используется Decoupled RL, который совместно оптимизирует бинарные суждения по подвопросам и глобальную оценку соответствия, что улучшает обобщение на out-of-domain задачи. Попарная верификация, при наличии ground-truth изображений, даёт более точные критики, чем поточечная, что подтверждено экспериментами на Maze и Sudoku. В итоге переход от генеративных моделей к агентам структурированного world modeling во многом зависит от качества попарных graded visual verifiers.

en.title: Revolutionizing Visual Verification with Pointwise Grading
en.desc: This paper introduces a new type of visual verifier that breaks down complex multimodal rules into smaller, pointwise scores instead of just giving a simple True/False answer. By using decoupled reinforcement learning, the verifier learns to improve its accuracy and generalization across different tasks. The approach allows for more detailed feedback, which helps the model understand and evaluate complex scenarios better. The results show that this method outperforms traditional binary verifiers, especially in structured tasks like Maze and Sudoku, highlighting the importance of accurate visual verification in multimodal intelligence.

zh.title: 分级视觉验证器：提升多模态智能的关键
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种分级视觉验证器，它将复杂的多模态规则分解为逐点评分，并利用解耦强化学习来提高模型的泛化能力。通过成对验证，进一步增强了结构化世界建模的准确性。与传统的二元验证器不同，这种新型验证器能够自动将复杂的提示或环境规则分解为细粒度组件，并提供连续的评分信号。实验结果表明，这种结构化和可解释的输出显著提高了验证器在不同领域的多模态任务中的泛化能力。

papers.title: Routing Policy Optimization for Online Diffusion Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract Routing Policy Optimization introduces stochastic attention routing inside diffusion generators to align them with reward signals while preserving the original deterministic sampler and improving training efficiency.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement learning can align visual generators with reward signals beyond their pretraining objectives, but existing score-function methods typically introduce stochasticity by perturbing the reverse denoising trajectory, leading to costly rollout-based optimization. We instead ask whether stochastic exploration can be introduced inside the generator while preserving its original sampler. Routing Policy Optimization (RPO) answers this question by turning attention routing into a stochastic exploration action. At a few selected denoising levels, each query block keeps its own block and samples further key blocks in proportion to the generator's native attention mass, or keeps dense attention. The sampled route perturbs the velocity of that transition, and a Gaussian likelihood around the dense velocity scores the perturbation with a score-function objective. RPO further uses a controlled two-rollout estimator: two rollouts share the same prompt, initial latent, routed denoising levels, and dense anchor layers, differing only in their sampled attention routes. Their reward difference provides an advantage signal for the routed transitions. Because the likelihood differentiates the dense velocity itself, the learned updates remain effective after routing is removed. At inference, RPO restores dense attention and retains the original deterministic sampler. Experiments on text-to-image and text-to-video generation show that RPO improves generation quality while achieving nearly 4x higher training efficiency than Flow-GRPO-style methods. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/rpo for visual results.

ru.title: Исследуем генератор изнутри: стохастическая маршрутизация attention ускоряет выравнивание диффузионных моделей
ru.desc: Статья представляет метод Routing Policy Optimization (RPO), который вводит стохастическую маршрутизацию attention внутри диффузионных генераторов, а не возмущает траекторию денойзинга. Для выбранных шагов денойзинга блоки запросов семплируют ключевые блоки пропорционально нативной attention-массе, а two-rollout оценщик с общим промптом и латентом даёт advantage-сигнал для reinforcement learning. Гауссово правдоподобие вокруг плотного velocity позволяет обучать модель с score-function целью так, что улучшения сохраняются без маршрутизации. На inference используется исходный детерминированный sampler с плотным attention, а эксперименты на text-to-image и text-to-video показывают лучшее качество и почти в 4 раза более высокую эффективность обучения по сравнению с Flow-GRPO.

en.title: Enhancing Generative Models with Stochastic Attention Routing
en.desc: This paper presents Routing Policy Optimization (RPO), a method that enhances diffusion generators by integrating stochastic attention routing while maintaining the original deterministic sampling process. By aligning visual generators with reward signals through controlled stochastic exploration, RPO improves training efficiency and generation quality. The approach utilizes a two-rollout estimator to provide an advantage signal based on the differences in sampled attention routes. Ultimately, RPO allows for effective updates during training and reverts to dense attention during inference, significantly outperforming existing methods in both text-to-image and text-to-video tasks.

zh.title: 路由策略优化：提升生成质量与训练效率的创新方法
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的路由策略优化方法，通过在扩散生成器中引入随机注意力路由，使其与奖励信号对齐，同时保持原有的确定性采样器，从而提高训练效率。该方法利用随机探索在生成器内部进行，而不是在反向去噪轨迹中引入随机性，从而避免了基于回滚的优化成本。通过在选定的去噪级别上，每个查询块保持自己的块，并根据生成器的原生注意力质量进一步采样关键块，来实现这一目标。实验结果表明，该方法在文本到图像和文本到视频生成任务中显著提高了生成质量，并且训练效率比传统方法高出近4倍。

papers.title: Trajectory-Level Speculation with Semantic Verification for Tool-Using Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract SpecAgent improves agent efficiency by having a small model draft tool-use steps that a large model verifies in parallel, reducing latency and memory use while preserving quality.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language model agents solve tasks through long sequences of tool calls, and the prevailing design has a single strong model generate every step, although many steps are routine enough for a much smaller model. Existing ways of sharing this work keep the strong model as the generator: routers and collaborative agents decide which model handles each query or step, and speculative methods check a small model's drafts one step at a time, usually against the strong model's own action. We introduce SpecAgent, a collaboration protocol that turns the strong model from the author of each step into a reviewer of steps drafted by a weak model. The weak model executes read-only tool calls as it drafts, so that every step is grounded in real observations, and holds the first action that would modify the environment. The strong model then verifies the drafted segment in a single prefill pass, commits the longest prefix it judges semantically valid, and repairs the first rejected step. Because verification replaces autoregressive decoding with parallel prefill, the strong model decodes only short verdicts and occasional repairs rather than every step. On τ^2-Bench, SpecAgent comes within one point of the strong model's success rate while roughly halving memory traffic and wall time, and on AutomationBench and VitaBench it recovers 44-75% of the quality gap while lowering both. In an edge-cloud deployment on MCP-Atlas with three cloud models, it closes 53-75% of the weak-strong quality gap while the strong model generates at most half as many tokens. These results suggest that a strong model need not author every step of an agent: reviewing grounded drafts retains most of its quality while cutting both latency and memory traffic.

ru.title: Большая модель проверяет, а не пишет каждый шаг агента
ru.desc: Статья предлагает SpecAgent: протокол, в котором небольшая модель (weak model) черновиком генерирует шаги агента, выполняя read-only вызовы инструментов, а большая модель (strong model) проверяет весь отрезок за один проход prefill. Большая модель принимает самый длинный корректный префикс и исправляет первый отклонённый шаг, поэтому она почти не декодирует токены. Такой подход сохраняет качество, близкое к большой модели, и заметно снижает задержку, объём памяти и число генерируемых токенов. Эксперименты на τ²-Bench, AutomationBench, VitaBench и MCP-Atlas подтверждают эффективность метода.

en.title: Efficient Collaboration: Small Drafts, Strong Reviews
en.desc: SpecAgent is a new approach that enhances the efficiency of language model agents by using a smaller model to draft tool-use steps, which are then verified by a larger model. This method reduces the time and memory needed for processing while maintaining high-quality outputs. Instead of having the strong model generate every step, it acts as a reviewer for the drafts created by the weak model, allowing for faster and more efficient task execution. The results show that SpecAgent significantly narrows the performance gap between the two models while decreasing resource usage.

zh.title: 高效代理：小模型草拟，大模型审核
zh.desc: SpecAgent通过让一个小模型草拟工具使用步骤，并由一个大模型并行验证，从而提高了代理的效率。这种方法减少了延迟和内存使用，同时保持了生成质量。与传统方法不同，SpecAgent将强模型的角色从每一步的生成者转变为草稿的审核者，使得每一步都基于真实观察。实验结果表明，SpecAgent在保持高质量的同时，显著降低了内存流量和处理时间。

papers.title: JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs
papers.abstract: Abstract A harness that delegates agent tool choices to small decision models via fitted confidence thresholds reduces cost and latency while preserving task success, supported by a new benchmark and a 4B model trained on agent error states.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Large language model (LLM) agents now fix software, operate computers and serve customers, but their harnesses, the programs that run them, call a large LLM at every step, which makes long tasks slow and costly. Most of these calls end in a multiple-choice decision, such as which tool to call next. Decision models such as Jev answer these questions directly, at a fraction of an LLM call's time and price. We ask how a harness can delegate these decisions to a decision model with little loss of success. To evaluate decision models in agentic tasks, we build AgentDecisionBench, which tests them from isolated questions up to control of a running agent, on public benchmarks and our DecisionGym environment. The decision model most accurate on isolated questions solved only 69.5% of agent tasks, and without a fitted confidence threshold, delegating tool choices lowered success by 19.0 points. Building on these findings, we then design JevAgentHarness, which fits this threshold for each choice on the agent's own trajectories and lets the LLM decide below it. Because existing decision models never see the states an agent reaches after its own mistakes, we train AgentDecision-4B, an open 4B model, on such states with Jev's answers as labels. On tasks unlike its training data, the agent solved 91.5% of them with AgentDecision-4B and 82.0% with Jev. On tasks like their training data, 4B models trained this way made agents 81.1-89.0% cheaper and up to 2.5 times faster, without losing 3 or more points of task success. The models, data, and harness will be released at https://github.com/JevAgentHarness/JevAgentHarness.

ru.title: Малые модели берут на себя рутинные решения агента — дешевле и быстрее, почти без потери качества
ru.desc: В статье описывается харнесс JevAgentHarness, который передаёт часть решений LLM-агента о выборе инструмента небольшим decision models с подобранным порогом уверенности. Авторы создают бенчмарк AgentDecisionBench для оценки таких моделей от изолированных вопросов до управления работающим агентом. Модель AgentDecision-4B обучается на состояниях, в которых агент совершает собственные ошибки, с разметкой ответами Jev. Результаты показывают, что стоимость работы агента снижается на 81–89%, а скорость растёт до 2.5 раз без существенной потери качества решения задач.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Efficient Decision-Making
en.desc: This paper introduces a new approach to improve the efficiency of large language model (LLM) agents by using smaller decision models to make tool choices. By implementing fitted confidence thresholds, the proposed JevAgentHarness reduces the number of costly LLM calls, thereby decreasing both latency and operational costs while maintaining high task success rates. The authors developed a benchmark called AgentDecisionBench to evaluate the performance of these decision models in various agentic tasks. Their findings show that the new harness can significantly enhance the speed and affordability of agent operations without compromising effectiveness.

zh.title: 智能决策，提升效率与成功率
zh.desc: 这篇论文提出了一种新的工具选择方法，通过小型决策模型和适应性置信阈值来降低成本和延迟，同时保持任务成功率。研究表明，传统的大型语言模型在每一步都调用会导致长任务变得缓慢和昂贵。通过构建AgentDecisionBench基准，评估决策模型在代理任务中的表现，发现适当的置信阈值可以显著提高成功率。最终，设计的JevAgentHarness能够在代理的轨迹上为每个选择调整阈值，从而实现更高效的决策过程。

papers.title: SWE-at-Scale: Scalable Issue Synthesis from Historical Bug Fixes
papers.abstract: Abstract SWE-at-Scale synthesizes realistic software engineering tasks by inverting real-world fixes to generate diverse, executable bugs for evaluating coding agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small As coding agents become increasingly capable, robust evaluation requires a broader and more diverse supply of verifiable software engineering (SWE) tasks. However, real-world tasks are constrained by the natural frequency of issue reporting and the substantial cost of manual curation. Furthermore, existing synthetic approaches rely primarily on the pretrained knowledge of large models coupled with heuristic prompting, often failing to capture the authentic, complex mechanics of software failures. To exponentially scale SWE task production, we introduce SWE-at-Scale, a framework that automatically synthesizes realistic issues by reverse-engineering real-world software fixes. Our key insight is that historical fixes encapsulate deep mechanistic knowledge of bug formation: inverting a fix transforms repair supervision into bug-induction supervision grounded in actual development scenarios. SWE-at-Scale transfers these learned bug patterns to novel code contexts, repeatedly sampling diverse bug typologies to construct executable SWE tasks. Extensive experiments show that SWE-at-Scale generates more diverse and realistic SWE tasks than current synthesis baselines while posing greater challenges to state-of-the-art coding agents. Notably, SWE-at-Scale can generate distinct bug types from a single code context, with bug diversity scaling robustly even up to 200 generations per file. Overall, SWE-at-Scale turns finite real-world fixes into reusable supervision for scalable synthesis of realistic, diverse, and challenging SWE tasks.

ru.title: Ошибки из прошлых исправлений — топливо для масштабной оценки AI-агентов
ru.desc: В статье представлен SWE-at-Scale — фреймворк для автоматической генерации реалистичных задач разработки ПО, предназначенных для оценки AI-агентов для написания кода. Ключевая идея заключается в обращении (inversion) реальных исправлений багов: из истории исправлений извлекаются закономерности возникновения ошибок, которые затем переносятся на новые фрагменты кода. Это позволяет создавать разнообразные исполняемые баги, которые сложнее для современных LLM-агентов, чем задачи, полученные с помощью простого промптинга. Эксперименты показывают, что метод масштабируется и генерирует до 200 различных багов на один файл.

en.title: Transforming Fixes into Diverse Bugs for Coding Agents
en.desc: SWE-at-Scale is a framework designed to create realistic software engineering tasks by reversing real-world software fixes to generate diverse bugs. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods that rely on large models and heuristic prompting, which often miss the complexity of actual software failures. By inverting fixes, SWE-at-Scale transforms the knowledge of how to repair software into a way to induce bugs, allowing for the creation of executable tasks that reflect real development scenarios. The framework demonstrates the ability to produce a wide variety of bug types from a single code context, significantly enhancing the evaluation of coding agents with more challenging and realistic tasks.

zh.title: SWE-at-Scale：自动合成多样化软件工程任务的框架
zh.desc: SWE-at-Scale 是一个框架，通过逆向工程真实世界的软件修复，自动合成现实的软件工程任务。它利用历史修复中的深层机制知识，将修复监督转化为基于实际开发场景的错误诱导监督。该框架能够在新的代码上下文中转移学习到的错误模式，生成多样化的可执行软件工程任务。实验表明，SWE-at-Scale 生成的任务比现有合成基线更具多样性和现实性，同时对最先进的编码代理提出了更大的挑战。

papers.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
papers.abstract: Abstract Velox accelerates long video rollouts by routing attention via geometric frustum slabs, reducing latency while preserving visual coherence.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by 4.36times and denoising by 2.43times. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.

ru.title: Быстрее генерировать долгие видео, помня, что уже показано
ru.desc: Статья представляет Velox — метод без дообучения, который ускоряет генерацию длинных видео в world models за счёт маршрутизации внимания по геометрическим срезам камеры (frustum slabs). Исторические блоки токенов описываются глубинными интервалами, а глубина текущего блока оценивается через multiwarp с приоритетом недавних кадров. В покрытых регионах пересечение срезов мягко корректирует важность блоков, определённую моделью, а в непокрытых сохраняется исходный маршрут без геометрического смещения. Метод совместим с FlashAttention-подобным блочным исполнением, и на chunk 48 даёт ускорение внимания в 4.36 раза и денойзинга в 2.43 раза при качестве, близком к плотной модели.

en.title: Accelerating Video Rollouts with Velox: Faster Attention, Coherent Visuals!
en.desc: Velox is a novel approach designed to enhance the efficiency of generating long video rollouts in interactive simulations. It utilizes geometric frustum slabs to optimize attention routing, which helps in reducing latency while maintaining visual coherence across generated content. By representing historical video segments as camera frustum slabs, Velox effectively manages context selection without the need for extensive training. This method significantly accelerates both attention processing and denoising, achieving notable speed improvements compared to traditional chunked video diffusion models.

zh.title: Velox：加速长视频生成的创新技术
zh.desc: Velox是一种加速长视频生成的技术，通过几何视锥体片段来优化注意力路由，从而减少延迟并保持视觉一致性。该方法利用视频世界模型，将动作和相机运动转化为长时间的视觉输出，使视频成为交互式模拟的自然界面。Velox通过区域级上下文选择的训练无关注意力路由器，解决了传统视频扩散模型在生成过程中保持上下文的瓶颈问题。实验结果表明，Velox在加速注意力和去噪方面显著提高了效率，展示了其在视频生成中的潜力。

papers.title: Do Better Visual Representations Always Lead to Better End-to-End Autonomous Driving?
papers.abstract: Abstract ViRA aligns visual foundation model representations with end-to-end driving planners to improve performance, showing that target selection and auxiliary perception supervision significantly affect planning gains.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Visual foundation models (VFMs) are increasingly integrated into end-to-end autonomous driving for their powerful representations, yet it remains unclear when these representations improve driving performance. To investigate this question, we introduce ViRA, a planner-agnostic visual representation alignment framework that keeps the planner architecture and inference cost unchanged. Our study reveals three findings: (1) VFM-guided visual representations consistently improve driving performance across diverse end-to-end planners, with gains extending to zero-shot closed-loop evaluation. (2) The choice of VFM target matters for planning performance, and alignment to a different VFM can further benefit planners with pre-trained VFM encoders. (3) Auxiliary perception supervision reduces sensitivity to VFM target selection, narrowing the EPDMS spread across five targets from 2.7 to 0.5 points and potentially compensating for less effective VFM targets. Guided by these findings, we develop ViRA-Diffusion, a diffusion-based planner trained without auxiliary perception supervision, which achieves 92.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest, outperforming recent methods in our comparison by at least 1.9 points. The results motivate jointly considering target selection and planner supervision when integrating VFMs into end-to-end autonomous driving. The results and demo are available at https://github.com/OpenDriveLab/ViRA.
affiliations: OpenDriveLab at The University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Умное зрение от фундаментальных моделей делает автопилот точнее, если правильно выбрать цель и supervision
ru.desc: Статья представляет ViRA — фреймворк выравнивания визуальных представлений (visual representation alignment), который переносит знания из visual foundation models (VFM) в end-to-end планировщики автономного вождения без изменения их архитектуры и стоимости inference. Авторы показывают, что такие VFM-направляемые представления стабильно улучшают качество планирования и работают даже в zero-shot closed-loop оценке, а выбор целевой VFM и вспомогательный supervision для задач восприятия существенно влияют на результат. Вспомогательная perception-supervision уменьшает чувствительность к выбору целевой VFM, а на основе выводов создан диффузионный планировщик ViRA-Diffusion без такого supervision. Модель достигает 92.3 EPDMS на NAVSIM v2 navtest, превосходя недавние методы как минимум на 1.9 пункта.

en.title: Enhancing Autonomous Driving with Visual Model Alignment
en.desc: ViRA is a framework designed to enhance the performance of end-to-end driving planners by aligning visual foundation model (VFM) representations. The study shows that using VFM-guided representations consistently improves driving outcomes across various planners, even in zero-shot scenarios. It also highlights the importance of selecting the right VFM target for optimal planning performance and how auxiliary perception supervision can mitigate the effects of poor target selection. The introduction of ViRA-Diffusion demonstrates significant improvements in driving performance, emphasizing the need to consider both target selection and planner supervision in autonomous driving systems.

zh.title: 优化自动驾驶的视觉表示对齐
zh.desc: ViRA是一个视觉表示对齐框架，旨在提高自动驾驶规划的性能。研究表明，视觉基础模型（VFM）能够显著改善多种端到端规划器的驾驶表现。选择合适的VFM目标对规划性能至关重要，而辅助感知监督可以减少对VFM目标选择的敏感性。通过这些发现，ViRA-Diffusion被开发出来，展示了在没有辅助感知监督的情况下也能取得优异的性能。

papers.title: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models
papers.abstract: Abstract SimVTA improves driving world action models by combining simulator-rendered video supervision with reinforcement learning trajectory optimization.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Driving world action models (WAMs) learn from paired trajectories and future observations. Post-training with reinforcement learning allows the policy to explore alternative trajectories and improve planning using driving rewards. However, driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectories, leaving these alternatives without corresponding visual supervision. Thus, we introduce SimVTA, a simulation-grounded post-training framework that combines trajectory optimization with video supervision. First, we sample candidate trajectories for each observation and use a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) to render future videos for high-reward candidates in real-world scenes reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). This provides trajectory-matched supervision independent of the model's own predictions. Under a limited rendering budget, we prioritize video supervision for higher-error futures among these rendered candidates. Finally, we optimize trajectory planning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and use a flow-matching loss on the matched videos to update shared representations. At inference time, the model predicts trajectories directly, without simulator calls. On NAVSIM v1, applying SimVTA to a WAM initialization improves PDMS from 86.2 to 91.3 (+5.1). It achieves 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 38.8 in closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM. Ablations show that updating shared representations with video supervision improves planning, while prioritizing higher-error futures among high-reward trajectories further improves performance.
affiliations: OpenDriveLab at The University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Видео для альтернативных траекторий делает автопилот умнее
ru.desc: В статье предлагается SimVTA — фреймворк пост-тренировки driving world action models, который сочетает оптимизацию траекторий через reinforcement learning (GRPO) с видеосупервизией. Для альтернативных траекторий симулятор (World Engine) на основе 3D Gaussian Splatting рендерит будущие видео, что даёт trajectory-matched supervision без опоры на собственные предсказания модели. При ограниченном бюджете рендеринга приоритет отдаётся траекториям с большей ошибкой, а flow-matching loss обновляет общие представления модели. На инференсе симулятор не нужен, а модель предсказывает траектории напрямую, при этом PDMS на NAVSIM v1 вырастает с 86.2 до 91.3.

en.title: Enhancing Driving Models with Simulated Video Supervision
en.desc: SimVTA is a framework that enhances driving world action models by integrating video supervision from simulations with reinforcement learning for better trajectory optimization. It generates future videos for high-reward candidate trajectories using a real-world simulator, allowing the model to learn from visual data that corresponds to potential future actions. This approach addresses the challenge of lacking visual supervision for alternative trajectories by prioritizing video rendering for those with higher prediction errors. The results show significant improvements in performance metrics, demonstrating that combining trajectory optimization with video supervision leads to more effective planning in driving scenarios.

zh.title: SimVTA：结合视频监督与强化学习的驾驶模型优化
zh.desc: SimVTA是一种改进驾驶世界动作模型的方法，它结合了模拟器生成的视频监督和强化学习轨迹优化。通过对配对轨迹和未来观察的学习，WAMs能够更好地理解驾驶场景。SimVTA通过在后期训练中使用视频监督，帮助模型探索替代轨迹并优化规划。实验结果表明，使用SimVTA后，模型在多个评估指标上都有显著提升。

papers.title: MFVSR: A Multi-Style and Fine-Grained Benchmark for Video Subtitle Removal
papers.abstract: Abstract MFVSR introduces a large-scale, multi-style benchmark for video subtitle removal that evaluates restoration fidelity, preservation, temporal consistency, and reliability through fine-grained, spatially decoupled protocols.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Video subtitle removal (VSR) is an important video restoration task, yet existing evaluation remains limited by low-resolution datasets, fragmented test sets, and generic video-inpainting protocols that fail to adequately capture localized restoration errors, unintended modifications, temporal instability, and incomplete outputs. In this paper, we introduce MFVSR, a large-scale multi-style benchmark for fine-grained and reliability-aware video subtitle removal evaluation. MFVSR distinguishes itself through three key features: (1) Large-scale and diverse data, comprising 3,000 paired videos from Real-HQ, Real-LQ, and AI-Generated sources, with an auxiliary set of 953 in-the-wild real videos for real-world coverage analysis; (2) Controlled subtitle diversity, spanning 16 languages and four factors covering spatial layout, temporal behavior, visual style, and language mode; (3) Fine-grained evaluation, introducing an information-conditioned, spatially decoupled protocol that separates blind from mask-guided removal and measures Restoration Fidelity, Preservation Fidelity, Temporal Fidelity, coverage, and failures. Experiments on six representative methods reveal substantial discrepancies between local restoration, outside-region preservation, temporal consistency, and full-set reliability that are obscured by conventional full-frame metrics. MFVSR therefore provides a more comprehensive and diagnostic foundation for evaluating and advancing video subtitle removal methods.
affiliations: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Честная оценка удаления субтитров: видим то, что скрывают обычные метрики
ru.desc: В статье представлен MFVSR — масштабный мультистилевой бенчмарк для удаления субтитров из видео, включающий 3000 парных видео из источников Real-HQ, Real-LQ и AI-Generated, а также 953 реальных видео. Бенчмарк охватывает 16 языков и четыре фактора разнообразия субтитров: пространственное расположение, временное поведение, визуальный стиль и языковой режим. Авторы предлагают детальный протокол оценки с пространственным разделением на blind и mask-guided удаление, измеряя Restoration Fidelity, Preservation Fidelity, Temporal Fidelity, покрытие и частоту сбоев. Эксперименты на шести репрезентативных методах показывают, что традиционные метрики на уровне всего кадра скрывают расхождения между локальным восстановлением, сохранением вне маски, временной согласованностью и надежностью.

en.title: Revolutionizing Video Subtitle Removal Evaluation with MFVSR
en.desc: The MFVSR paper presents a new benchmark for evaluating video subtitle removal, focusing on restoration quality and consistency. It addresses limitations in current methods by providing a large dataset of 3,000 paired videos and an additional 953 real-world videos for better analysis. The benchmark includes diverse subtitle styles across multiple languages and evaluates performance using a detailed protocol that distinguishes between different types of restoration tasks. This comprehensive approach allows for a more accurate assessment of video subtitle removal techniques, highlighting areas for improvement in existing methods.

zh.title: MFVSR：视频字幕去除的新标准
zh.desc: MFVSR是一个大规模的多风格基准，用于评估视频字幕去除的效果。它通过细致的空间解耦协议，考察恢复的保真度、保持性、时间一致性和可靠性。该基准包含3000对视频，涵盖多种语言和视觉风格，提供了丰富的数据集。通过引入信息条件的评估方法，MFVSR能够更准确地测量去除效果，帮助改进视频字幕去除技术。

papers.title: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
papers.abstract: Abstract A team of autonomous AI agents used an open research system to independently post-train a small base model into a cross-domain generalist that matched or exceeded its official instruction-tuned version.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence. We study a weaker form that can be measured today: frontier agents post-training a small raw base model with public data, as a test of their research potential. We build Athanor, an open agent-native system for autonomous post-training research (AutoPostTrain) on real GPUs. We give the agents full research autonomy, low-friction engineering tools, and efficient starter code. The agents carry out the research themselves: they read datasets and evaluation results, build their training data, write and modify training algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and analyze the results to decide what to try next. They work in a sandbox and cannot use external teacher models. Athanor's services supply frozen evaluation, managed jobs, decontaminated data, a persistent research record, and a held-out suite the agents are unaware of. In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, each on an eight-GPU node and given no research advice, improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a six-task development suite and from 9.2 to 48.2 on a held-out suite, against 66.5 and 47.9 for the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain generalist model that matches or surpasses the official instruct version on average. The campaign's full record shows that the agents reach this level by recombining known methods and each other's models: SFT on public reasoning data, RL with a rollout change one agent introduced, weight merges across agents, and rounds of self-distillation. With execution handled, today's agents already have the engineering and research ability to conquer this task. We hope Athanor provides a foundation for scaling autonomous AI research.

ru.title: Агенты сами обучают LLM не хуже официальной версии
ru.desc: Авторы показывают, что команда из четырёх автономных AI-агентов может самостоятельно выполнить post-training маленькой базовой LLM, превратив её в универсального генералиста. Для этого создана система Athanor, где агенты сами читают данные, пишут обучающие алгоритмы, подбирают гиперпараметры и анализируют результаты, без внешних teacher-моделей. За 104 часа модель Qwen3-4B-Base по среднему качеству на скрытом наборе тестов сравнялась с официальной instruct-версией, используя SFT, RL, weight merges и self-distillation. Главный вывод: современные агенты уже способны к автоматизированным исследованиям в ML, а такой подход может стать основой для масштабируемого автономного AI-исследования.

en.title: Empowering AI Agents for Autonomous Model Improvement
en.desc: This paper presents a system called Athanor, which enables autonomous AI agents to post-train a small base model into a more capable cross-domain generalist model. The agents operate independently, utilizing public data to enhance their performance without external guidance, demonstrating a form of recursive self-improvement. Over a 104-hour campaign, these agents significantly improved the model's performance metrics, surpassing the official instruction-tuned version. The study highlights the potential of autonomous AI in conducting research and model training, paving the way for future advancements in AI capabilities.

zh.title: 自主AI研究的新里程碑
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种名为Athanor的开放式自主研究系统，旨在让人工智能代理独立进行后训练。研究团队通过让四个Claude Opus 5.5代理在没有外部指导的情况下，利用公共数据对一个小型基础模型进行训练，成功将其性能提升到与官方版本相当或更高的水平。代理们能够自主读取数据集、构建训练数据、调整超参数，并分析结果以决定下一步的研究方向。该研究展示了自主AI系统在机器学习领域的潜力，尤其是在跨领域通用模型的构建上。

papers.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
papers.abstract: Abstract Market-based post-training jointly learns decentralized agent policies and self-orchestration via bidding, improving coordination, scalability, and robustness across embodied and research tasks.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt together without a central coordinating agent. We evaluate MPT on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research. Results show gains over monolithic post-training and confirm that agent participation indeed evolves with learning. With the same post-trained action policies, learned self-orchestration outperforms alternative coordination strategies. Ablations show that both action and bidding benefit from learning, and that learned bids provide more effective action-training signals. Beyond the original training objectives, trained swarms adapt faster to related tasks and achieve better performance with larger populations at inference time. Larger populations also suffer smaller performance losses under agent dropout, demonstrating that learned self-orchestration supports reuse, scaling, and robustness in decentralized agent swarms. Code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Embodied-Minds-Lab/MPT.

ru.title: Рынок ставок учит рой агентов работать вместе без центрального управления
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод market-based post-training (MPT), который совместно обучает действия децентрализованных агентов и их самоорганизацию через систему ставок. Агенты выражают готовность участвовать с помощью bids, и эти ставки определяют, кто будет действовать, а коллективный результат даёт локальный training credit. Такой подход, без центрального координирующего агента, улучшает координацию, масштабируемость и устойчивость роя, что подтверждено экспериментами с embodied crafting, навигацией роботов и deep research. Обученные рои быстрее адаптируются к новым задачам и лучше работают при большем числе агентов и при выбытии части из них.

en.title: Empowering Agent Swarms through Market-Based Learning
en.desc: This paper presents a new approach called market-based post-training (MPT) for improving how decentralized agent swarms learn and coordinate their actions. Instead of training agents in fixed roles, MPT allows agents to bid for participation, which helps them learn both their individual tasks and how to work together more effectively. The results show that this method enhances coordination, scalability, and robustness, allowing swarms to adapt quickly to new tasks and perform better even when some agents drop out. Overall, MPT demonstrates that learning both action policies and self-orchestration together leads to more efficient and resilient multi-agent systems.

zh.title: 市场基础后训练：提升代理群体的协调与鲁棒性
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种市场基础的后训练框架（MPT），用于联合学习去中心化代理群体的行动策略和自我编排。通过出价，代理表达参与意愿，从而决定谁执行任务以及如何通过集体结果提供本地训练反馈。MPT的评估结果显示，与传统的单一后训练方法相比，代理的参与度随着学习而演变，且学习的自我编排在协调策略上表现更优。该框架在多个任务中表现出更好的适应性和鲁棒性，尤其是在代理数量增加时，性能损失更小。

papers.title: CarryOn: A Dual-Loop Harness for Personalized and Reliable Robot Assistance
papers.abstract: Abstract CarryOn enhances frozen vision-language-action policies with persistent personalized planning and supervised execution with recovery skills to improve safety and adaptability.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small While generalist vision-language-action (VLA) models have enabled diverse open-world manipulation, real-world robotic assistance requires two critical capabilities they currently lack: personalization and reliable execution. First, executing an instruction like "make me a sandwich" requires grounding subtask decomposition in persistent user preferences rather than relying on a single generic solution. Second, reliable deployment demands explainable safety assurance that proactively prevents hazards and gracefully recovers from occasional physical failures. To address these gaps, we present CarryOn, a dual-loop harness designed to augment a frozen VLA policy. The planning loop maintains persistent user-level and scene-level context that is continually grounded against new observations and revised through interaction, enabling personalized task selection and execution grounding across conversations and changing scenes. The execution loop actively supervises policy rollouts, shielding actions from predicted hazardous contact. When execution fails, the system invokes reusable control-based recovery skills that restore task progress and are refined through reflection on earlier failures. On a real robot and in simulation, CarryOn dispatches preference-consistent subtasks across users and scenes, reduces the violation rate of an already safety-finetuned VLA from 52.6% to 6.1%, and increases recovery success from 13% to 80% when refined skills are reused.

ru.title: Персональный и безопасный робот-помощник: CarryOn учится помнить и восстанавливаться
ru.desc: Статья представляет CarryOn — надстройку над замороженной моделью vision-language-action (VLA), которая добавляет персонализацию и надёжное исполнение задач роботом. Контур планирования хранит постоянный контекст пользователя и сцены, который обновляется по новым наблюдениям и позволяет выбирать подзадачи с учётом предпочтений. Контур исполнения контролирует действия политики и блокирует опасные контакты, а при сбоях запускает повторно используемые навыки восстановления, которые улучшаются через рефлексию. Эксперименты на реальном роботе и в симуляции показывают снижение доли нарушений безопасности с 52.6% до 6.1% и рост успешного восстановления с 13% до 80%.

en.title: Personalized Robotics: Safe and Adaptive Task Execution
en.desc: CarryOn is a system that improves robotic assistance by enhancing frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policies with personalized planning and execution skills. It focuses on understanding user preferences to break down tasks into subtasks that are tailored to individual needs, rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach. The system also ensures safety by supervising actions to prevent accidents and by employing recovery skills when things go wrong. In tests, CarryOn significantly reduced safety violations and improved the success rate of recovering from failures, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world scenarios.

zh.title: 个性化规划与安全执行的智能助手
zh.desc: CarryOn 是一种增强冻结的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略的方法，旨在通过持久的个性化规划和监督执行来提高安全性和适应性。该系统能够根据用户的偏好持续调整任务选择，并在执行过程中提供安全保障，防止潜在的危险。它通过双循环设计，结合用户和场景的上下文信息，确保任务执行的个性化和可靠性。当执行失败时，CarryOn 能够调用可重用的恢复技能，帮助系统恢复任务进度。实验结果表明，CarryOn 显著降低了安全违规率，并提高了恢复成功率。

papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.abstract: Abstract Virtual Head Attention improves long-context model efficiency by reducing KV cache and compute while preserving quality through lightweight linear query and output transformations.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank I + AB^top residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale (+0.05\% to +0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by 4times vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and 2times vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, S{=}4096). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by +0.70\,/\,+2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.

ru.title: Больше виртуальных голов — меньше памяти, то же качество
ru.desc: В статье представлен метод Virtual Head Attention (VHA) для механизма внимания в LLM с длинным контекстом. Он решает проблему «невозможного треугольника»: одновременно уменьшает размер KV cache, вычисления при обучении и prefill, сохраняя качество модели. Метод использует два легковесных линейных преобразования: Q Premix для восстановления разнообразия виртуальных голов и Linear Postmix для объединения признаков между головами через низкоранговую структуру. Благодаря отсутствию нелинейностей VHA сводится к стандартной архитектуре GQA-2 и превосходит GQA по качеству при меньшем объёме кэша и вычислений.

en.title: Efficient Long-Context Attention with Virtual Head Optimization
en.desc: Virtual Head Attention (VHA) enhances the efficiency of long-context models by optimizing the key-value (KV) cache and computational requirements while maintaining high model quality. It addresses the trade-offs in attention mechanisms, known as the 'impossible triangle', by introducing two lightweight linear transformations: Q Premix and Linear Postmix. These operations allow for better utilization of query heads and inter-head features without adding complexity, making it compatible with existing GQA optimizations. As a result, VHA significantly reduces KV cache size and computational load while consistently outperforming standard GQA models across various scales.

zh.title: 虚拟头注意力：提升长上下文模型效率的创新方案
zh.desc: 虚拟头注意力（VHA）通过减少键值缓存（KV cache）和计算量，提高了长上下文模型的效率，同时保持了模型质量。该方法采用轻量级的线性查询和输出变换，解决了长上下文大语言模型中KV缓存大小、训练和预填充计算量与模型质量之间的“不可调和三角”问题。VHA通过两个轻量级线性操作，改善了这三个方面的性能，具体包括对查询的近似恒等变换和通过低秩残差结构融合头部特征。实验结果表明，VHA在多个规模上均超越了标准GQA基线，同时显著降低了KV缓存和计算开销。

papers.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
papers.abstract: Abstract CoDA co-evolves a simulation engine and robot policy via shared memory of failures and progress, using vision-language diagnostics and staged potential rewards to improve out-of-distribution manipulation success.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

ru.title: Робот учится на своих ошибках: симуляция и политика развиваются вместе
ru.desc: Статья представляет CoDA — фреймворк, в котором симуляционный движок и политика робота (action policy) совместно эволюционируют через общую память ошибок и прогресса обучения. Vision-language критик диагностирует провалы политики, а эти диагнозы превращаются в программы генерации сложных сред и программы обучения. Метод Text2potential переводит диагнозы в стадийные потенциалы (staged potentials) для обучения ценности action-chunk, обеспечивая плотный сигнал без искажения оптимальной политики. На задачах манипуляции успешность на out-of-distribution данных выросла с 5.3% до 27.6%, а на LIBERO-Pro — до 84% и 76% при возмущениях позиции и инструкции.

en.title: CoDA: Co-evolving Simulation and Robot Learning for Enhanced Performance
en.desc: The paper introduces CoDA, a framework that enhances robot learning by co-evolving a simulation engine and a robot policy. It utilizes a shared memory system that records failures and progress, allowing the robot to learn from its mistakes. By employing vision-language diagnostics, CoDA generates tailored training environments that specifically address the robot's weaknesses.
