The framework significantly improves the robot's performance in out-of-distribution tasks, demonstrating a notable increase in success rates through iterative training and environment refinement.

zh.title: CoDA：提升机器人操作成功率的创新框架
zh.desc: CoDA是一种框架，通过共享的异构记忆共同进化模拟引擎和机器人策略，以提高机器人在不同环境下的操作成功率。它利用视觉-语言诊断和分阶段潜在奖励来识别和解决策略的失败。通过将诊断转化为行动价值学习的潜在阶段，CoDA为策略更新提供了密集的监督，同时保持任务的最优策略。实验结果表明，CoDA在四个操作任务中显著提高了机器人在不熟悉环境中的成功率。

papers.title: Beyond Policy Rollouts: Embedding-Space Directional Exploration with Anchored Noise for LLM RLVR
papers.abstract: Abstract EDEN improves reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by injecting anchored embedding noise into rollout conditioning to increase diversity and strengthen group-relative advantage signals without altering inference.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically uses small rollout groups per prompt, where repeated sampling from the same policy can yield highly similar trajectories, reducing within-group reward variation and weakening group-relative advantage signals. Existing remedies such as higher sampling temperature, entropy bonuses, asymmetric clipping, and larger rollout budgets broaden sampling or modify policy updates but leave rollout conditioning unchanged. In this paper, we propose EDEN (Embedding-space Directional Exploration via anchored Noise), which intervenes at the rollout source through anchored input perturbations. EDEN explores beyond the policy's own rollouts. Within the same rollout budget, it replaces a small fraction of standard rollouts in each group with rollouts that the same policy generates from the prompt plus a single appended, perturbed embedding position, rather than from the prompt alone. Gaussian noise drives variation, while a shared anchor provides a common conditioning direction within each prompt group. Selected perturbed rollouts contribute to GRPO updates with downweighted advantages, and the model architecture, discrete decoding, and test-time inference remain unchanged. Across model scales and mathematical reasoning benchmarks, EDEN outperforms GRPO and the exploration controls evaluated in the same pipeline, with the largest gains in sampled solution coverage. Analyses show that more prompt groups provide non-zero group-relative learning signals and that noise and anchoring play complementary roles. Intervening at the rollout source is thus an effective lever for exploration in RLVR.
affiliations: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)

ru.title: Исследуй пространство эмбеддингов, а не только собственные ответы
ru.desc: Статья предлагает метод EDEN для обучения с подкреплением по верифицируемым наградам (RLVR), где в небольших группах ответов на один промпт модель часто генерирует похожие траектории. EDEN решает это, заменяя часть обычных rollout-ов теми, что генерируются с добавлением одного шумного эмбеддинга, зафиксированного общим якорем для группы. Такие rollout-ы участвуют в обновлениях GRPO с уменьшенными advantage, при этом архитектура модели и инференс не меняются. Эксперименты на задачах математического рассуждения показывают улучшение над GRPO, особенно в покрытии найденных решений.

en.title: EDEN: Enhancing Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Noise
en.desc: The paper introduces EDEN, a method that enhances reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by adding noise to the input embeddings during the rollout process. This approach increases the diversity of sampled trajectories, which helps to improve the group-relative advantage signals without changing the underlying model architecture. By perturbing the input embeddings, EDEN allows the policy to explore beyond its typical rollouts, leading to better performance on various benchmarks. The results show that this method significantly outperforms existing techniques by improving solution coverage and maintaining effective learning signals across different prompt groups.

zh.title: EDEN：通过锚定噪声增强强化学习的多样性
zh.desc: EDEN是一种改进强化学习的方法，通过在回滚条件中注入锚定嵌入噪声来增强多样性和强化组相对优势信号，而不改变推理过程。传统的可验证奖励强化学习通常使用小的回滚组，这导致重复采样产生高度相似的轨迹，从而降低组内奖励的变化。EDEN通过在回滚源头进行干预，使用锚定输入扰动来探索超出策略自身的回滚。实验结果表明，EDEN在多个模型规模和数学推理基准上优于现有方法，尤其在采样解决方案覆盖率方面取得了显著提升。

papers.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
papers.abstract: Abstract FlashMask-3 accelerates long-context attention via a Hopper-optimized sparse-mask kernel and distributed context-parallel extensions that eliminate mask-communication overhead and improve training throughput.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-context training of large language and multimodal models couples structured attention masks (document, prefix-LM, share-question, sliding-window, block-sparse) with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compresses them from O(n^2) to O(n) via four query-axis boundary vectors, covering broad structured patterns. Implemented for Ampere GPUs, it neither exploits FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline on Hopper nor supports distribution. The column-wise sparse mask is indexed by key positions but stores query-axis interval boundaries. Under any multi-chunk context-parallel assignment, it reduces per-rank mask localization to a provably zero-communication clip--shift--max on the boundary vectors, compatible with the single-GPU kernel. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with three-role warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a mask-aware distributed extension: zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer (HCC-IPO), and a mask-aware compute-communication overlap with mask-driven communication pruning, whose forward all-gather uses topology-aware hierarchical routing. On a single H100 across 12 masks at 4K--128K context, it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45--141%, 34--71%, and 2--44%. At context-parallel degrees 4--32 with 8K sequence per device, it attains 31--75% compute-communication overlap efficiency and improves throughput over Megatron-Core CP ring, Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and MagiAttention by 1.80times--3.71times, 1.71times--2.92times, and 1.09times--1.46times. In end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs, it raises throughput by 7.3--11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline, with attention forward+backward 24.5--44.9% faster.

ru.title: Маска без лишних коммуникаций ускоряет обучение длинному контексту
ru.desc: Статья представляет FlashMask-3, оптимизированное ядро внимания (attention kernel) для архитектуры Hopper GPU с поддержкой разреженных масок и распределённого обучения через context parallelism. Ключевая идея: column-wise sparse mask хранит границы интервалов по оси запросов, что позволяет локализовать маску на каждом узле без коммуникаций. Добавлены warp specialization поверх пайплайна FlashAttention-3, балансировщик нагрузки HCC-IPO и перекрытие вычислений с коммуникациями с учётом маски. На практике это даёт прирост TFLOPs на одном H100 и ускорение обучения LLM-модели 118B-A14B MoE на 128K контексте.

en.title: Accelerating Long-Context Attention with FlashMask-3
en.desc: FlashMask-3 is a machine learning framework designed to enhance the efficiency of long-context attention mechanisms in large language and multimodal models. It introduces a Hopper-optimized sparse-mask kernel that significantly reduces the computational complexity of attention masks from O(n^2) to O(n) by utilizing column-wise sparse masks. This innovation allows for improved training throughput by minimizing mask-communication overhead and enabling effective multi-node context parallelism. The framework demonstrates substantial performance gains, achieving higher TFLOPs and compute-communication overlap efficiency compared to existing methods, thereby accelerating the training of large models.

zh.title: FlashMask-3：加速长上下文注意力的革命性技术
zh.desc: FlashMask-3 是一种加速长上下文注意力的技术，利用 Hopper 优化的稀疏掩码内核和分布式上下文并行扩展，消除了掩码通信开销，提高了训练吞吐量。它通过四个查询轴边界向量将结构化注意力掩码的复杂度从 O(n^2) 压缩到 O(n)，覆盖广泛的结构模式。FlashMask-3 在单个 H100 GPU 上实现了显著的性能提升，尤其是在多掩码和大上下文的情况下，提升了计算与通信的重叠效率。最终，在大规模模型的端到端训练中，FlashMask-3 提高了吞吐量，并加快了注意力的前向和反向计算速度。

papers.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
papers.abstract: Abstract SUPRA-Tex decouples visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and 3D completion to generate relightable 3D materials that preserve reference image details and complete unobserved surfaces.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Single image 3D generation aims to dress a given 3D mesh with relightable materials while faithfully preserving the visual details of a reference image. Existing methods either introduce artifacts when fusing inconsistent multi-view predictions or struggle to preserve fine details through implicit image-feature conditioning. To resolve these challenges, we introduce SUPRA-Tex, built on the principle of decoupling visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion. This division of labor allows the 3D generator, trained on limited 3D data, to focus its capacity on preserving visible evidence and completing unobserved surfaces. Specifically, we first train an MLLM-based image editing model to predict lighting-separated PBR maps in the reference view. We then project these maps onto the visible surface and encode them with the pretrained material VAE encoder into native observation latents that share the generation target's latent space. An interleaved flow transformer holds these latents as fixed, read-only anchors while alternating unobserved-region and full-surface updates to generate complete material latents. This design achieves super-alignment with the reference, delivering What You See Is What You Get fidelity on visible regions and coherent completion on unobserved surfaces. Trained solely on public datasets, SUPRA-Tex achieves SOTA performance in both geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end asset generation, matching or even exceeding leading commercial systems on in-the-wild images. Project page: https://supra-3d.github.io/supratex/
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Видишь то, что получишь: 3D-материалы, точно повторяющие референс
ru.desc: SUPRA-Tex — это метод генерации 3D-материалов по одному изображению, который разделяет задачу на три части: оценку видимых PBR-материалов, выравнивание поверхности и восстановление невидимых областей. Сначала MLLM-based модель редактирования изображений предсказывает PBR-карты с отделённым освещением, которые проецируются на видимую поверхность и кодируются материальным VAE в латентные представления. Затем interleaved flow transformer использует эти латенты как фиксированные якоря и генерирует полные материальные латенты, обеспечивая высокую точность на видимых участках и согласованное заполнение скрытых. Обучение проводится только на открытых датасетах, а результаты сопоставимы или превосходят коммерческие системы на реальных изображениях.

en.title: Decoupling for Detail: SUPRA-Tex Revolutionizes 3D Material Generation
en.desc: SUPRA-Tex is a novel approach in 3D material generation that separates the tasks of estimating visible materials, aligning surfaces, and completing 3D structures. By decoupling these processes, it effectively preserves the details from reference images while filling in unseen areas of a 3D mesh. The method utilizes a machine learning model to create physically-based rendering (PBR) maps that are then projected onto the 3D surface, ensuring high fidelity and coherence. This technique not only enhances the quality of generated materials but also achieves state-of-the-art results using only publicly available datasets.

zh.title: SUPRA-Tex：超对齐的三维材料生成
zh.desc: SUPRA-Tex 是一种新方法，它将可见材料估计、表面对齐和三维补全分开处理，以生成可重新照明的三维材料，同时保留参考图像的细节。该方法通过训练一个基于机器学习的图像编辑模型，预测参考视图中的光照分离的 PBR 地图，并将这些地图投影到可见表面上。SUPRA-Tex 通过交替更新未观察区域和完整表面，生成完整的材料潜变量，从而实现与参考图像的超对齐。经过训练，SUPRA-Tex 在几何条件纹理化和端到端资产生成方面达到了最先进的性能，甚至在实际图像上超越了领先的商业系统。

papers.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
papers.abstract: Abstract Cowork-Gym synthesizes collaborative agent environments via iterative validation and trains Qwen models that substantially improve agentic benchmark performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Cowork agents navigate dependencies across tools and files while adapting to changing user requirements and edits to shared workspaces. Scaling such environments requires maintaining consistency among task objectives, executable resources, user behavior, and success criteria. We introduce Cowork-Gym, a framework that synthesizes Cowork environments through a build-execute-revise loop that uses execution evidence and review feedback to validate and repair generated environments. To capture realistic Cowork dynamics, a stateful user simulator responds to the agent's actions through dialogue and direct edits to the shared workspace. We synthesize 64.9K environments across 14 application scenarios and use them to post-train 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B Qwen models with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation. Averaged across six agentic benchmarks, these models outperform their corresponding base checkpoints by 8.7, 6.4, and 4.1 points, respectively. Ours-27B ranks second overall among the evaluated models and achieves the highest average scores on PawBench and ClawEval, outperforming models with over 100B total parameters on both benchmarks.

ru.title: Масштабируем совместную работу AI-агентов с помощью автоматически синтезированных сред
ru.desc: Статья представляет Cowork-Gym — фреймворк, который автоматически синтезирует среды для совместной работы AI-агентов с инструментами и файлами. Среды создаются циклом build-execute-revise, где результаты выполнения и ревью используются для валидации и исправления сгенерированных сред. Stateful симулятор пользователя реагирует на действия агента через диалог и прямые правки общего рабочего пространства, имитируя реалистичную динамику. На основе 64.9K сред авторы делают post-training моделей Qwen (9B, 27B, 35B-A3B) с помощью SFT, RL и on-policy distillation, что повышает результаты на шести агентных бенчмарках, а модель 27B превосходит модели более 100B параметров на PawBench и ClawEval.

en.title: Empowering Agents with Cowork-Gym: Adaptive Learning in Collaborative Environments
en.desc: The paper introduces Cowork-Gym, a framework designed to create collaborative agent environments that adapt to user needs and changes in shared workspaces. It employs a build-execute-revise loop to ensure that the generated environments are validated and refined based on execution evidence and user feedback. By synthesizing a large number of environments, the framework enables the training of Qwen models, which significantly enhance performance on agentic benchmarks. The results show that these models outperform larger counterparts, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Cowork-Gym approach in improving agent capabilities.

zh.title: Cowork-Gym：提升协作代理性能的创新框架
zh.desc: Cowork-Gym 是一个用于合成协作代理环境的框架，通过迭代验证来训练 Qwen 模型，从而显著提高代理基准性能。该框架能够在工具和文件之间导航，同时适应用户需求和共享工作空间的变化。为了保持任务目标、可执行资源、用户行为和成功标准的一致性，Cowork-Gym 采用构建-执行-修订的循环，通过执行证据和反馈来验证和修复生成的环境。我们合成了 64.9K 个环境，并使用这些环境对 Qwen 模型进行后训练，结果显示这些模型在多个基准测试中表现优异。

papers.title: Memory as Weights: Internalizing Long-Term History for Streaming Videos
papers.abstract: Abstract MaLoW internalizes streaming video history into evolving LoRA weights via a recurrent HyperNetwork, improving streaming vision-language performance with minimal latency overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

ru.title: История видео хранится в весах, а не в контексте
ru.desc: В статье предлагается MaLoW — фреймворк для стриминговых vision-language моделей (VLM), который хранит историю видео не в контексте, а во весах. Рекуррентная HyperNetwork постепенно сворачивает поступающие видеонаблюдения в LoRA-веса фиксированного размера, поэтому не нужно заново обрабатывать весь видеопоток. Для обучения авторы собрали датасет MaLoW-Instruct из 381K пар вопрос-ответ по 56K видео. На бенчмарке OVO-Bench (backward split) метод превосходит прежние подходы с памятью на 3,9–11,8%, а также улучшает успешность действий в vision-language-action моделях на 9,3%.

en.title: MaLoW: Streamlining Memory for Enhanced Video Understanding
en.desc: The paper introduces MaLoW, a novel framework for streaming vision-language models that efficiently integrates historical video data into lightweight parameter updates. Instead of competing for context, MaLoW internalizes past observations into evolving LoRA weights using a recurrent HyperNetwork, allowing for seamless incorporation of historical context. This approach minimizes latency while enhancing performance on various benchmarks, demonstrating significant improvements over traditional memory mechanisms. Additionally, MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale dataset, supports training and showcases the framework's versatility in both video understanding and vision-language-action tasks.

zh.title: MaLoW：流媒体记忆的新突破
zh.desc: MaLoW是一种流媒体记忆框架，通过递归超网络将历史视频信息内化为不断演变的轻量级参数更新，从而提高流媒体视觉语言模型的性能。与传统的记忆机制不同，MaLoW将历史上下文转化为权重，避免了历史信息与当前观察之间的竞争。该方法允许在不重新访问完整视频流的情况下，逐步整合视频观察。通过构建大规模的流媒体视频数据集MaLoW-Instruct，研究表明MaLoW在多个基准测试中表现优异，且延迟开销较小。

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract LEASH is a training-free framework that uses latent uncertainty to escalate from a weak to a strong computer-use agent only when needed and monitors the strong agent afterward, reducing cost while maintaining high success.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Computer-use agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks, where running a frontier model at every step is expensive and a small open-weight model alone often fails. Weak-to-strong escalation offers a middle ground where a weak agent acts by default and hands control to a strong one only when needed. The core challenge is deciding when to escalate, which requires an uncertainty signal cheap enough to check at every step. However, even after handoff, the strong agent can still get lost, but a black-box API that the strong agent is usually served exposes no internals to monitor. To this end, we propose LEASH, a training-free framework that unleashes the strong agent only when the weak agent's latent uncertainty signals it is needed, and keeps it on a leash afterward. LEASH has three layers: (1) initial task uncertainty for early routing, (2) step-level uncertainty for runtime escalation, and, after handoff, (3) a shadow observer for continued oversight of the strong black-box agent. Here, we use latent uncertainty as a fuel for all three layers. Specifically, we compare the weak model's hidden states with those from its past successful and failed trajectories, and a state that looks more like the failures signals higher uncertainty. During weak-agent execution, our uncertainty estimator reuses activations already produced during action generation, so it needs no extra forward pass or dedicated monitor training. Experiments on OSWorld across four contemporary model backbones show that LEASH consistently improves over standalone weak agents and outperforms random escalation by 6.55--11.94 points at matched escalation rates. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, LEASH achieves 73.66% task success at $0.4117 per task, matching always-on Claude Opus 5 (72.90%) while reducing inference cost by 19.2%.

ru.title: Сильный агент — только когда нужен, и всегда под присмотром
ru.desc: Статья представляет LEASH — фреймворк без дополнительного обучения, который передаёт управление от слабого computer-use агента сильному только тогда, когда латентная неопределённость слабого агента указывает на необходимость. Неопределённость оценивается сравнением скрытых состояний модели с состояниями из прошлых успешных и неуспешных траекторий, и это переиспользует активации, уже полученные при генерации действий, без дополнительного прохода. После передачи управления «теневой наблюдатель» контролирует чёрный ящик сильного агента, не имея доступа к его внутренностям. Эксперименты на OSWorld показывают, что LEASH превосходит случайную эскалацию на 6.55–11.94 пункта и при этом сохраняет высокую успешность, снижая стоимость вывода на 19.2%.

en.title: Smart Escalation: Using Uncertainty to Optimize Agent Performance
en.desc: LEASH is a novel framework designed to optimize the performance of computer-use agents by leveraging latent uncertainty to transition from a weak agent to a strong agent only when necessary. This approach minimizes costs associated with running a powerful model continuously while ensuring high success rates in long-horizon tasks. The framework consists of three layers: initial task uncertainty for routing, step-level uncertainty for real-time escalation, and a shadow observer for monitoring the strong agent post-handoff. Experiments demonstrate that LEASH significantly outperforms traditional methods, achieving higher task success rates and reduced inference costs.

zh.title: LEASH：智能代理的灵活升级与监控
zh.desc: LEASH是一个无训练的框架，利用潜在的不确定性在需要时将计算机使用代理从弱变强，并在之后进行监控，从而降低成本并保持高成功率。该框架通过弱到强的升级策略，默认使用弱代理，只有在必要时才交给强代理控制。LEASH的核心挑战是决定何时升级，这需要一个足够便宜的、不确定性信号来在每一步进行检查。实验结果表明，LEASH在多个模型基础上表现优于单独的弱代理，并在匹配的升级率下超越随机升级。

papers.title: Calibrated Typed Decisions for Entity, Relation, and Event Extraction
papers.abstract: Abstract CalOn is a compact unified encoder that jointly performs entity, relation, and event extraction across diverse schemas by encoding text with type definitions and using shared probabilistic reasoning over combined type evidence.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Information extraction models often perform well on the datasets they are trained on, but transferring to new domains and annotation guidelines remains challenging. Supporting user-specified types alone does not resolve this problem. We present CalOn, a unified 0.6B-parameter encoder for entity, relation, and event extraction across datasets and schemas. The model jointly encodes text and type definitions, then directly identifies entity spans, relations between spans, and event triggers and arguments. Its extraction decisions consider the requested types together, using their combined evidence to identify relevant candidates before assigning a type. This gives all three tasks a common probabilistic formulation while keeping every extracted mention anchored to the input text. We train on diverse sources, and supplement supervised learning with a reward that encourages correct extractions and penalises incorrect ones. Across 40 benchmarks, CalOn outperforms the evaluated baselines on most benchmarks. It leads all reported relation extraction benchmarks and achieves the highest average F1 for event triggers and arguments with gold triggers. The same model also performs strongly on aspect sentiment triplet extraction and pronoun resolution through its span-pair formulation. A correction for the probability bias introduced during training improves confidence estimates for entities, relations, and event arguments after calibration, with little change in F1.

ru.title: Один энкодер для сущностей, отношений и событий: универсальное извлечение информации
ru.desc: В статье представлен CalOn — компактный унифицированный энкодер с 0.6 млрд параметров для извлечения сущностей, отношений и событий. Модель совместно кодирует текст и определения типов, а решения о извлечении принимаются на основе объединённых признаков через общую вероятностную модель. Обучение использует разнообразные датасеты и дополнительный reward, поощряющий правильные и штрафующий ошибочные извлечения. CalOn превосходит базовые модели на большинстве из 40 бенчмарков, а коррекция смещения вероятностей улучшает калибровку уверенности модели.

en.title: CalOn: Unified Extraction for Entities, Relations, and Events
en.desc: CalOn is a unified encoder designed for extracting entities, relations, and events from text across various schemas. It utilizes a compact architecture with 0.6 billion parameters, allowing it to jointly process text and type definitions for improved extraction accuracy. By employing shared probabilistic reasoning, CalOn effectively integrates evidence from multiple tasks, enhancing its ability to identify relevant candidates for extraction. The model demonstrates superior performance across 40 benchmarks, particularly excelling in relation extraction and event argument identification, while also addressing probability bias for better confidence estimates.

zh.title: CalOn：统一的实体、关系与事件提取编码器
zh.desc: CalOn是一种紧凑的统一编码器，能够在不同的模式下共同执行实体、关系和事件提取。它通过编码文本和类型定义，并利用共享的概率推理来处理组合类型证据。该模型在多种数据集上进行训练，并通过奖励机制来鼓励正确的提取结果。CalOn在40个基准测试中表现优异，尤其在关系提取和事件触发器的提取上取得了最高的F1分数。

papers.title: Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers
papers.abstract: Abstract Gen4P repurposes a pretrained video generator into a feed-forward 4D perceiver that predicts geometry and motion from monocular video via on-demand cross-attention decoding and frozen depth priors.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We introduce Gen4P, a unified framework for recovering 4D geometry and motion from monocular video. We show that a pretrained video generator can be repurposed into a feed-forward 4D perceiver without iterative denoising. Building on on-demand querying, Gen4P processes clean video latents in a single encoder pass and predicts the requested 4D attributes through a lightweight cross-attention decoder. The on-demand query formulation enables flexible spatial sampling, and our proposed continuous-time queries further provide temporal flexibility. To strengthen geometric knowledge, we propose a straightforward plug-in solution by incorporating a pretrained video-depth LoRA as a frozen geometry prior, improving overall performance without adding extra trainable parameters. Gen4P achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on tasks of 3D point tracking, video depth and camera pose estimation. Qualitative results on in-the-wild videos illustrate its capability of tracking complex motion while maintaining the delicate structure. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of video generative pretraining for unified 4D perception. See https://gen4p.github.io for more visual results.

ru.title: Генеративная видео-модель становится универсальным 4D-перцептором
ru.desc: Gen4P — это единая модель, которая восстанавливает 4D-геометрию и движение по обычному монокулярному видео. Авторы адаптируют предобученный video generator в feed-forward перцептор: вместо итеративного denoising чистые video latents обрабатываются за один проход энкодера. Легковесный cross-attention декодер отвечает на запросы (on-demand queries), включая непрерывные временные запросы, а замороженный video-depth LoRA используется как геометрический prior без дополнительных обучаемых параметров. Модель показывает результаты уровня state-of-the-art или конкурентные результаты в 3D point tracking, оценке глубины видео и позы камеры.

en.title: Transforming Video Generation into 4D Perception
en.desc: Gen4P is a novel framework that transforms a pretrained video generator into a 4D perceiver, allowing it to predict geometry and motion from single-camera video inputs. It utilizes a feed-forward architecture that avoids the need for iterative denoising, making the process more efficient. By employing on-demand cross-attention decoding and leveraging frozen depth priors, Gen4P can flexibly sample spatially and temporally. The framework achieves impressive results in tasks like 3D point tracking and camera pose estimation, showcasing the effectiveness of video generative pretraining for advanced 4D perception.

zh.title: 视频生成预训练，开启四维感知新篇章
zh.desc: Gen4P是一个统一框架，能够从单目视频中恢复四维几何和运动。它利用预训练的视频生成器，转变为一个前馈的四维感知器，能够通过按需交叉注意解码和固定深度先验进行预测。该方法通过单次编码处理干净的视频潜在特征，并通过轻量级的交叉注意解码器预测所需的四维属性。Gen4P在3D点跟踪、视频深度和相机姿态估计等任务上表现出色，展示了视频生成预训练在统一四维感知中的潜力。

papers.title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Abstract SERO improves long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning by training on executable oracle continuations from real policy states, weighted by policy compatibility, without inference-time overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-horizon agentic RL is constrained by the futures visited by the current policy. When rollouts fail to reach useful behaviors, improved credit assignment cannot provide supervision for states and actions that were never encountered. On-policy distillation (OPD) introduces teacher guidance on policy-induced states, and recent multi-turn variants improve how this guidance is scheduled, replayed, refined, or validated. However, they do not directly use the oracle-controlled future itself as the training trajectory. We introduce State-Rooted Executable Rollout Optimization (SERO), which augments on-policy agentic RL with executable oracle continuations. SERO restores a state actually reached by the current policy and lets a training-only oracle continue interacting with the real environment, making the downstream observations and oracle actions themselves available for learning. It then applies policy-reachability weighting, which weights each oracle step by the frozen behavior policy's compatibility with the preceding oracle actions. This allows deeper supervision to become effective as the policy becomes more compatible with the oracle branch. The oracle loss is optimized separately from the base RL estimator and no oracle is used at inference time. We evaluate SERO on two challenging interactive-agent benchmarks, ALFWorld and WebShop, using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. On ALFWorld, learning the full executable continuation is substantially more effective than supervising only the root oracle action, while policy-reachability weighting further improves out-of-distribution performance.

ru.title: Учимся на продолжениях эксперта из реально достигнутых состояний
ru.desc: В статье представлен метод SERO, который улучшает обучение с подкреплением (RL) для агентов с длинным горизонтом планирования. Вместо того чтобы опираться только на траектории текущей политики, метод восстанавливает реально достигнутое состояние и позволяет обучающему оракулу продолжать взаимодействие со средой, а полученные наблюдения и действия используются для обучения. Для каждого шага оракула применяется взвешивание по достижимости политики, учитывающее совместимость замороженной поведенческой политики с предыдущими действиями оракула, что делает глубокую супервизию эффективнее. Оракул используется только при обучении и не требуется при инференсе, а эксперименты на ALFWorld и WebShop с моделями Qwen2.5 показывают улучшение, особенно на out-of-distribution задачах.

en.title: Enhancing Long-Horizon RL with Oracle Continuations
en.desc: The paper presents SERO, a method that enhances long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning by utilizing executable oracle continuations from real policy states. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional methods that struggle with credit assignment when rollouts do not reach useful behaviors. By incorporating policy-reachability weighting, SERO ensures that the training focuses on actions that are compatible with the current policy, allowing for more effective learning. The results demonstrate that SERO significantly improves performance on interactive-agent benchmarks compared to previous methods.

zh.title: SERO：提升长时间代理强化学习的有效性
zh.desc: SERO是一种改进长时间代理强化学习的方法，它通过从真实策略状态中训练可执行的oracle延续来实现，而无需在推理时增加开销。该方法解决了当前策略访问的未来限制问题，使得在未遇到的状态和动作上无法提供有效的监督。SERO通过恢复当前策略实际达到的状态，并让训练专用的oracle继续与真实环境交互，从而使下游观察和oracle动作可用于学习。通过应用策略可达性加权，SERO能够在策略与oracle分支兼容性增强时，使得更深层次的监督变得有效。

papers.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract MMSearch-OPD improves long-horizon multimodal search by refining reasoning data and jointly training with reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback.   We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds.   Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

ru.title: Учим мультимодальных агентов долго и настойчиво искать ответы
ru.desc: В статье представлен метод MMSearch-OPD для обучения мультимодальных агентов глубокого поиска, которые решают задачи с длинными цепочками рассуждений. Авторы предлагают конвейер Refine, который расширяет простые мультимодальные вопросы в сложные цепочки рассуждений, управляя глубиной поиска и требованиями к кросс-модальным доказательствам. Обучение объединяет reinforcement learning с наградой за ответ и on-policy distillation, где учитель корректирует токен-уровневые ошибки ученика, а коэффициент дистилляции экспоненциально затухает. Эксперименты показывают прирост качества от очистки данных и дополнительное улучшение после совместного обучения поверх SFT.

en.title: Enhancing Long-Horizon Multimodal Search with MMSearch-OPD
en.desc: MMSearch-OPD enhances long-horizon multimodal search by refining the reasoning data used in the process. It employs a combination of reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD) to improve the training of agents that handle complex queries. The method includes a Refine pipeline that expands reasoning chains from simple multimodal questions, allowing for deeper searches and better evidence gathering. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach leads to significant improvements in the capabilities of multimodal deep search agents.

zh.title: 提升长时间多模态搜索能力的创新方法
zh.desc: MMSearch-OPD是一种改进长时间多模态搜索的方法，通过精炼推理数据并结合强化学习和在线蒸馏进行联合训练。该方法通过扩展现有简单多模态问题的推理链，来提高搜索的深度和跨模态证据的要求。训练过程中，答案奖励和轻量级行为惩罚引导强化学习，而奖励差距则调节对不完美学生轨迹的教师指导。实验结果表明，数据精炼和联合训练后，长时间多模态深度搜索能力得到了显著提升。

papers.title: WorldMemBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Memory of Video World Models
papers.abstract: Abstract WorldMemBench evaluates world memory in video models by testing static and dynamic retention across repeated revisits and state transitions.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small As video models enable longer and more realistic interactive experiences, maintaining a world consistent with its history becomes essential. This requires both preserving previously observed content and ensuring coherent world evolution over time. World memory is a critical capability to evaluate alongside visual fidelity and video duration. We introduce WorldMemBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating world memory in video world models. Across 260 test cases, it assesses static memory through the retention of human identity and appearance, object appearance and geometry, and environmental content and geometry, and dynamic memory through event progression and state persistence. Using controlled camera departures and multi-revisit trajectories, the benchmark evaluates static content against fixed initial references and dynamic events against expected state transitions. It combines appearance and geometry metrics with event-specific assessments, and reports video quality and camera-following accuracy as complementary diagnostics. Evaluation of nine representative models shows that strong static retention does not imply reliable dynamic state evolution, while repeated revisits reveal memory degradation beyond the first return. Human studies support the alignment between our automatic evaluations and human judgments. WorldMemBench provides a systematic testbed for diagnosing memory failures and guiding the development of persistent, temporally coherent video worlds.

ru.title: Помнит ли видео-мир своё прошлое? Проверяем память генеративных моделей
ru.desc: WorldMemBench — это новый бенчмарк для оценки памяти мира (world memory) в видео-моделях, которые генерируют интерактивные миры. Он проверяет статическую память, то есть сохранение внешности людей, объектов и окружения, а также динамическую память, то есть корректное развитие событий и сохранение состояний. Тестирование проводится на 260 кейсах с контролируемыми уходами камеры и многократными возвратами к одним и тем же локациям, а качество измеряется метриками внешнего вида, геометрии и специфичными для событий проверками. Эксперименты с девятью моделями показали, что хорошая статическая память не гарантирует надёжной динамики состояний, а при повторных возвратах память заметно деградирует.

en.title: Evaluating Memory in Video Models for Coherent Experiences
en.desc: WorldMemBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate how well video models retain and evolve their world memory during interactions. It tests both static memory, which includes the retention of identities, objects, and environments, and dynamic memory, which focuses on how events progress and states persist over time. The benchmark uses a variety of test cases to assess memory retention and coherence, revealing that strong static memory does not guarantee effective dynamic state transitions. By comparing automatic evaluations with human judgments, WorldMemBench aims to identify memory failures and improve the consistency of video worlds.

zh.title: 评估视频模型中的世界记忆
zh.desc: WorldMemBench 是一个用于评估视频模型中世界记忆的基准工具。它通过测试静态和动态记忆在重复访问和状态转换中的保持能力，来确保视频世界与其历史的一致性。该基准涵盖了260个测试案例，评估人类身份、物体外观和环境内容的静态记忆，以及事件进展和状态持久性的动态记忆。研究表明，强大的静态记忆并不一定意味着动态状态的可靠演变，且重复访问会导致记忆衰退。

papers.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: Abstract CLIFT uses conformal self-verification to convert sparse judge feedback into reusable training rewards and judge-free test-time trajectory selection for open-source web agents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Open-source web agents are now strong enough to execute realistic browser tasks, but training them with reinforcement learning still depends on weak supervision: binary task success is too sparse for credit assignment, while frontier-language-model judges are too expensive to call at every step and cannot be assumed available at deployment. We introduce CLIFT, a training and test-time scaling method built around conformal self-verification. During training, the agent answers natural-language verification questions about its own rollouts; a Compositional Conformal Certifier keeps only question signals whose URL-conditional evidence agrees with a training-time judge, assigns signed trust weights through polarity-aware lift, and blends the resulting verifier score into per-step rewards in a way that never subtracts from the judge baseline. At test time, the same certified bank is frozen and reused as structured evidence for Conformal Trajectory Selection (CTS): the agent samples a greedy rollout and one or more diverse retries, the self-verifier summarises each URL trace, and a conservative majority-vote rule chooses whether to swap away from the current incumbent without calling any external judge. This single mechanism supports three settings. On WebArena Infinity, CLIFT achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source web agents. On VisualWebArena, a bank trained with the open model transfers to GPT-5.5 at test time and reaches state-of-the-art performance under the canonical harness. On Online Mind2Web, without training an agent on the benchmark, translating the certified question bank improves a live-web agent in zero-shot evaluation. Together these results position conformal self-verification as a way to turn costly judge feedback into a reusable training signal and a judge-free test-time scaling signal.

ru.title: Самопроверка агента вместо дорогого судьи: дешевле обучение и умнее выбор действий
ru.desc: Статья представляет CLIFT — метод обучения веб-агентов с помощью reinforcement learning, в котором агент сам задаёт себе верификационные вопросы о своих траекториях. Compositional Conformal Certifier отбирает только те сигналы, которые согласуются с внешним LLM-judge, и присваивает им взвешенное доверие, что превращает редкий бинарный сигнал успеха в плотные награды за каждый шаг. На этапе инференса тот же откалиброванный набор вопросов используется для Conformal Trajectory Selection: агент выбирает лучшую из нескольких попыток по majority-vote без обращения к дорогому judge. Метод показывает state-of-the-art результаты на WebArena Infinity и VisualWebArena и улучшает zero-shot работу агента на Online Mind2Web.

en.title: Transforming Sparse Feedback into Powerful Training Signals with CLIFT
en.desc: CLIFT is a novel method that enhances the training of open-source web agents by using conformal self-verification to transform sparse feedback into effective training rewards. It allows agents to evaluate their own actions through natural-language questions, which helps in assigning trust weights to their decisions without relying heavily on external judges. During testing, CLIFT utilizes a certified bank of evidence to select the best trajectories without needing additional judge input, thus streamlining the process. This approach not only improves performance on various benchmarks but also demonstrates the potential of self-verification in reinforcement learning.

zh.title: CLIFT：将评估反馈转化为可重用的训练信号
zh.desc: CLIFT是一种利用符合性自我验证的方法，将稀疏的评估反馈转化为可重复使用的训练奖励，并在测试时选择轨迹而无需评估者。该方法通过让智能体回答自然语言验证问题来进行训练，并使用组合符合性认证器来评估这些问题的信号。CLIFT在测试时利用冻结的认证银行作为结构化证据，选择最佳轨迹而不需要外部评估者的调用。实验结果表明，CLIFT在多个开放源代码网络代理的任务中表现出色，展示了符合性自我验证在训练和测试中的有效性。

papers.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models
papers.abstract: Abstract MSR improves generative diversity by mining categorical schemas from real artifacts to guide conditional rendering at test time.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Modern generative models produce high-quality individual outputs but struggle to sample diversely, even when explicitly instructed to do so. We introduce MINE-SAMPLE-RENDER (MSR), a test-time approach that externalizes the diversity into an explicit, corpus-derived sampling procedure. Our pipeline (i) mines an interpretable categorical schema from a corpus of real artifacts and supplies statistics for sampling; (ii) samples attribute configurations from the corpus-derived statistics; (iii) uses a generative model purely as a conditional renderer of a sampled configuration. Across weather report generation, user simulation, webpage design, text-to-image generation, and agent-generated 3D assets, we evaluate the diversity and output quality of MSR-guided generation and show that MSR improves alignment with corpus distributions and diversity of generated outputs.

ru.title: Разнообразие генерации выносим в явный сэмплинг по данным
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод MINE-SAMPLE-RENDER (MSR), который повышает разнообразие генерации в современных генеративных моделях. Сначала из корпуса реальных артефактов автоматически извлекается интерпретируемая категориальная схема и статистика для сэмплирования. Затем на основе этой статистики выбираются конфигурации атрибутов, а сама LLM или генеративная модель используется лишь как условный рендерер заданной конфигурации. Эксперименты на задачах генерации прогнозов погоды, симуляции пользователей, дизайна веб-страниц, text-to-image и 3D-ассетов показывают, что MSR улучшает соответствие распределениям корпуса и разнообразие результатов.

en.title: Enhancing Generative Diversity with MSR
en.desc: The paper introduces MINE-SAMPLE-RENDER (MSR), a method that enhances the diversity of outputs generated by machine learning models. It does this by creating a categorical schema from real-world data, which helps guide the sampling process during generation. By using this schema, MSR allows for more varied attribute configurations to be sampled, leading to richer and more diverse outputs. The approach is tested across various applications, demonstrating improved alignment with real-world distributions and increased output diversity.

zh.title: 提升生成多样性的MSR方法
zh.desc: MSR（MINE-SAMPLE-RENDER）是一种在测试时提高生成多样性的方法。它通过从真实物品中挖掘类别模式来指导条件渲染，从而改善生成模型的输出多样性。该方法首先从语料库中提取可解释的类别模式，并提供采样统计信息；然后根据这些统计信息进行属性配置的采样；最后，使用生成模型作为条件渲染器来生成样本配置。通过在天气报告生成、用户模拟、网页设计、文本到图像生成和代理生成的3D资产等任务中评估，MSR显示出在生成输出的多样性和质量方面的显著提升。

papers.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
papers.abstract: Abstract LeanPRM uses the Lean proof assistant to automatically generate step-level correctness labels for natural-language mathematical proofs, enabling scalable training of learned verifiers without human annotation.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small AI systems now write long and difficult mathematical proofs, and checking their step-by-step validity is becoming a bottleneck. A learned verifier could check proofs cheaply, but training one requires a correctness label on every step, and such labels are hard to obtain for open-ended proofs. Existing methods take them from human annotators, which is costly, or derive them from final answers, which proofs do not have, and formalizing each proof in Lean requires expert effort. We introduce LeanPRM, a framework that uses the Lean proof assistant to create step-level labels for natural-language proofs. A model writes a natural-language proof together with a paired formal proof, without feedback from Lean. Lean then labels every step, and a second model discards failures caused only by the formal syntax, so that the negative labels mark errors in the mathematics. LeanPRM contains 10,634 proofs with 152K labeled steps and no human annotation. A Qwen3-4B verifier trained on LeanPRM raises exact step-label accuracy on a held-out set of 200 proofs (LeanPRM-Bench) from 48.2 to 74.7, as opposed to 60.3 when the same base model is trained on PRM800K. It also selects better proofs in best-of-N selection on IMO-level problems, and outperforms the PRM800K-trained verifier on three of four external verification benchmarks. Training on LeanPRM improves verifiers at every size from 0.6B to 8B parameters on LeanPRM-Bench, Hard2Verify and IMO-GradingBench. Given the labels need no human annotation, LeanPRM can grow with the supply of formal statements, offering a path to step-level feedback on AI-generated proofs that are hard for humans to check.

ru.title: Lean размечает доказательства, а не люди
ru.desc: В статье представлен LeanPRM — фреймворк, который использует Lean proof assistant для автоматической генерации пошаговых меток корректности для доказательств на естественном языке без участия людей. Модель пишет неформальное доказательство вместе с парным формальным, Lean размечает каждый шаг, а вторая модель отбрасывает ошибки, связанные только с синтаксисом, оставляя негативные метки лишь для реальных математических ошибок. На основе этого создан датасет из 10 634 доказательств и 152 тысяч размеченных шагов. Verifier на базе Qwen3-4B, обученный на LeanPRM, заметно превосходит версию, обученную на PRM800K, на бенчмарке LeanPRM-Bench и масштабируется от 0.6B до 8B параметров.

en.title: Automating Proof Verification with LeanPRM
en.desc: LeanPRM is a framework that automates the generation of correctness labels for each step in natural-language mathematical proofs using the Lean proof assistant. This approach addresses the challenge of training learned verifiers, which require accurate step-level labels that are typically difficult and costly to obtain from human annotators. By leveraging Lean, the framework produces a large dataset of labeled proofs without human intervention, enabling scalable training of AI models. The results show significant improvements in verification accuracy and performance on various benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of LeanPRM in enhancing the reliability of AI-generated mathematical proofs.

zh.title: LeanPRM：自动生成数学证明的正确性标签
zh.desc: LeanPRM 是一个框架，利用 Lean 证明助手自动生成自然语言数学证明的逐步正确性标签。这使得训练学习型验证器变得可扩展，而无需人工标注。通过生成的标签，模型可以有效地检查数学证明的每一步，解决了传统方法中人工标注成本高和难以获取的问题。LeanPRM 包含超过 10,000 个证明和 152,000 个标注步骤，显著提高了验证器的准确性和性能。

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract Copy-Paste Language Models enhance in-context copying by adding a lightweight head that improves training efficiency, downstream performance, and long-context retrieval with minimal overhead.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.

ru.title: Явное моделирование копирования делает LLM эффективнее
ru.desc: В статье предлагаются Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLM), которые дополняют стандартную LM-голову лёгкой Copy-Paste головой для улучшения копирования из контекста. Такой подход повышает эффективность обучения, качество на downstream-задачах и результаты в задачах с длинным контекстом и retrieval. Эксперименты с предобучением моделей от 135M до 1.7B параметров показывают улучшения на всех масштабах и архитектурах при минимальных накладных расходах. Авторы объясняют эффект тем, что CPLM частично смягчает узкое место градиента LM-головы за счёт альтернативного пути градиента.

en.title: Enhancing Copying Efficiency in Language Models with CPLMs
en.desc: This paper introduces Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which enhance the ability of language models to copy information from their inputs. By adding a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the traditional language modeling head, CPLMs improve training efficiency and performance in downstream tasks. The authors demonstrate that this approach allows for better handling of long-context scenarios and retrieval tasks with minimal additional computational cost. The success of CPLMs is attributed to their ability to alleviate the gradient bottleneck typically faced by standard language models.

zh.title: 提升上下文复制能力的复制-粘贴语言模型
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的语言模型，称为复制-粘贴语言模型（CPLMs），通过在传统语言模型头部添加轻量级的复制-粘贴头来增强上下文复制能力。CPLMs在训练效率、下游性能和长上下文检索方面表现出显著的改进。我们通过对135M到1.7B参数的模型进行预训练，验证了该方法在各个规模和基础架构上的有效性。研究表明，CPLMs通过提供替代的梯度路径，部分缓解了语言模型头的梯度瓶颈，从而实现了更好的性能。

papers.title: Recursive Environment Scaling for General Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract Recursive Environment Scaling transforms benchmarks to increase difficulty while preserving objectives, improving both agent evaluation and supervised fine-tuning performance.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small We study environment scaling as a way to increase agent-benchmark difficulty while holding core task objectives fixed. Our framework, Recursive Environment Scaling (RES), transforms existing benchmark environments while preserving their objectives and completion requirements. A proposer changes information access, resource relations, and execution dependencies; execution-grounded checks validate the resulting candidate, and accepted changes are inherited across rounds. This produces related environments for paired evaluation and training-trajectory collection. Experiments on 294 initial tasks from three benchmarks show lower task success for all six evaluation models, with decreases of 57.14--77.14 percentage points on Claw-Eval-Live. With equal trajectory counts and identical optimization settings, fine-tuning on RES trajectories outperforms original-trajectory SFT in all nine model--benchmark comparisons by 7.00--14.61 percentage points. Ablations identify recursive inheritance and dependency composition as important contributors to increased difficulty. Together, these results support environment scaling for both agent evaluation and training.

ru.title: Усложняй среду, а не цель: масштабирование окружений для обучения и оценки LLM-агентов
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают Recursive Environment Scaling (RES) — метод, который усложняет существующие бенчмарки для AI-агентов, не меняя их основную цель. Предлагающая модель (proposer) изменяет доступ к информации, связи между ресурсами и зависимости выполнения, а проверка на основе реального выполнения отбирает корректные варианты. Принятые изменения наследуются между раундами, создавая связанные среды для парной оценки и сбора траекторий обучения. Эксперименты показывают, что успешность агентов падает, а дообучение (SFT) на траекториях RES превосходит обучение на исходных траекториях во всех сравнениях.

en.title: Scaling Challenges for Smarter Agents
en.desc: The paper introduces Recursive Environment Scaling (RES), a method that modifies existing benchmarks to make them more challenging while keeping the main objectives intact. This approach allows for better evaluation of agents and enhances their performance during supervised fine-tuning. By altering aspects like information access and resource relations, RES creates new environments that help in training and evaluating agents more effectively. Experiments show that agents trained on these modified environments perform better than those trained on original benchmarks, highlighting the benefits of environment scaling in machine learning.

zh.title: 递归环境扩展：提升智能体评估与训练的利器
zh.desc: 递归环境扩展（RES）是一种通过改变基准测试的难度来提高智能体评估和监督微调性能的方法。该框架在保持核心任务目标不变的情况下，转变现有的基准环境。通过改变信息访问、资源关系和执行依赖关系，生成相关环境以进行配对评估和训练轨迹收集。实验结果表明，使用RES轨迹进行微调的模型在所有比较中表现优于原始轨迹，支持了环境扩展在智能体评估和训练中的有效性。

papers.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
papers.abstract: Abstract  We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Complex real-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long-horizon coding and multi-agent coordination. We describe the setup, how the run unfolded, the team's strategies (dividing the work, sharing what they learned, recovering each other's items), and the limits of the result.

ru.title: Четыре ИИ-агента самостоятельно победили Эндер-дракона в Minecraft
ru.desc: Исследователи запустили четыре LLM-агента Gemini 4 Argon в песочнице Minecraft с единственной целью: победить Эндер-дракона. Агенты управляли персонажами через библиотеку Mineflayer, координировались в чате и общей памяти, сами планировали, писали и отлаживали код без ролей и игровой логики, заданных людьми. За 27 часов и 14 минут они написали 2783 программы и победили дракона, погибнув 605 раз, что стало первым полностью автономным прохождением Minecraft с помощью AI. Результат показывает, что агенты способны поддерживать связный план из тысяч зависимых шагов, а это важно и для сложных реальных задач разработки ПО.

en.title: Autonomous AI Agents Conquer Minecraft's Ender Dragon!
en.desc: This paper presents an innovative approach where four AI agents, using the Mineflayer library, autonomously collaborated to defeat the Ender Dragon in Minecraft. The agents demonstrated advanced problem-solving skills by planning, coding, and debugging their strategies without human intervention. Over the course of 27 hours, they created 2,783 programs, showcasing their ability to manage complex tasks and coordinate effectively as a team. This achievement highlights the potential of AI in tackling long-term projects that require sustained collaboration and adaptability, similar to challenges faced in real-world software engineering.

zh.title: AI智能体在Minecraft中自主击败末影龙
zh.desc: 本文介绍了四个Gemini 4 Argon智能体在Minecraft生存世界中合作击败末影龙的过程。这些智能体通过开源库Mineflayer控制玩家，并通过游戏内聊天和共享内存进行协调。研究人员可以实时观察整个过程，但没有干预的必要。最终，智能体在27小时14分钟内编写了2783个程序，成功完成了这一任务，展示了AI在复杂任务中的自主能力和多智能体协作的潜力。

papers.title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Abstract PN-Mix improves low-bit KV cache quantization by identifying salient RoPE channel pairs via query-key norms, achieving strong accuracy at lower bit rates.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Long-output inference in large language models suffers from severe KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. While KV cache quantization alleviates this issue, low-bit quantization (e.g., 2-bit) severely degrades model accuracy. Recent mixed-precision key-cache quantization methods mitigate this degradation by allocating higher precision to important key channels, but estimate channel saliency using only key statistics. Through attention logit perturbation analysis at the RoPE channel-pair level, we show that quantization errors in channel pairs with large query--key pair-norm products contribute significantly to logit variation. Based on this insight, we propose PN-Mix, a mixed-precision key-cache quantization method for RoPE-based decoder-only LLMs, which allocates higher precision to salient channel pairs identified once during the prefill stage and reused throughout decoding. Across standard reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks, PN-Mix with 2.26-bit average precision achieves comparable or better average accuracy than prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32--2.39 bits. Furthermore, in our Pareto sweep, PN-Mix degrades gracefully down to 1.5 bits, whereas the compared baselines exhibit sharper performance drops below 2.25 bits.

ru.title: Точность там, где она действительно нужна: умное сжатие KV-кэша без потери качества
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают PN-Mix — метод смешанной точности для квантизации KV-кэша в LLM на основе RoPE, где проблема в том, что при 2-битной квантизации точность модели сильно падает. Ключевая идея: ошибки квантизации пар каналов с большим произведением норм query и key сильнее всего влияют на логиты внessions внимания, поэтому именно эти пары получают повышенную точность. Важные каналы определяются один раз на этапе prefill и переиспользуются при декодировании. В экспериментах PN-Mix при 2.26 бита даёт сопоставимую или лучшую точность, чем базовые методы при 2.32–2.39 бита, и деградирует плавнее вплоть до 1.5 бит.

en.title: Optimizing KV Cache with Smart Channel Pair Selection
en.desc: The paper introduces PN-Mix, a method that enhances low-bit quantization of key-value (KV) caches in language models by focusing on important channel pairs identified through query-key norms. This approach addresses the challenge of maintaining model accuracy while reducing memory and bandwidth usage during inference. By analyzing logit variations at the RoPE channel-pair level, PN-Mix allocates higher precision to the most salient channels, improving performance even at lower bit rates. The results show that PN-Mix achieves competitive accuracy compared to existing methods while allowing for more efficient quantization.

zh.title: PN-Mix：低比特量化的精度提升
zh.desc: PN-Mix是一种改进低比特KV缓存量化的方法，通过查询-键范数识别显著的RoPE通道对，从而在较低比特率下实现强大的准确性。虽然KV缓存量化可以缓解内存和带宽瓶颈，但低比特量化（例如2比特）会严重降低模型的准确性。PN-Mix通过在预填充阶段识别重要通道对，并在解码过程中重复使用，分配更高的精度来解决这一问题。实验结果表明，PN-Mix在多个基准测试中表现出与之前的混合精度方法相当或更好的准确性，同时在比特数降低时性能下降更为平缓。

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.abstract: Abstract The study proposes an automated weak-to-strong loop that hardens agent environment verifiers against reward hacking by iteratively finding and repairing vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Agent environments are essential for large language model (LLM) development. They use programmatic verifiers to turn complex outcomes into rewards. Verifiers can be attacked into awarding full credit to cheating agents without completing the intended task, causing inaccurate evaluation and misalignment in training. As agent environments scale in numbers and difficulty, so must the repairing of exploitable verifiers. To this end, we ask whether today's model with scaled compute can automatically harden agent environments to prevent potentially stronger future models from reward hacking. We introduce a scalable, fully automatic approach to weak-to-strong verifier hardening. It first sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify, then uses a hacker-fixer loop to find and repair remaining verifier vulnerabilities.   We apply this loop to Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA, substantially reducing attack success across these agent environments. The iterative design scales with the hardening budget, producing progressively stronger defenses as the number of loop iterations increases and outperforming the static, non-iterative baseline. An earlier version of our hacker-fixer loop has been adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository as a way to audit exploits in its environments. Project page: https://verifier-hardening.github.io/.

ru.title: Самоукрепляющиеся верификаторы: ИИ защищает ИИ от взлома наград
ru.desc: Статья предлагает автоматический цикл «слабый-к-сильному» для защиты верификаторов агентных сред от reward hacking, когда агент получает награду, не выполнив задачу. Верификатор помещается в изолированную песочницу, которую агент не может изменить. Затем цикл hacker-fixer итеративно ищет уязвимости и исправляет их, используя LLM. Метод протестирован на Terminal Bench, KernelBench и SETA и заметно снижает успешность атак, а качество защиты растёт с числом итераций.

en.title: Strengthening Verifiers Against Reward Hacking with Automated Loops
en.desc: This paper presents a method to strengthen agent environment verifiers against reward hacking, which occurs when agents manipulate the system to gain rewards without completing tasks. The proposed automated weak-to-strong loop iteratively identifies and fixes vulnerabilities in isolated sandboxes, ensuring that verifiers remain robust as agent environments become more complex. By applying this approach to various benchmarks, the authors demonstrate a significant reduction in the success of attacks on these environments. The method scales effectively, providing stronger defenses with each iteration, and has been recognized for its utility in auditing exploits.

zh.title: 自动化增强代理环境，防止奖励黑客行为
zh.desc: 本研究提出了一种自动化的弱到强的循环机制，用于增强代理环境验证器，以防止奖励黑客行为。该方法通过在隔离的沙箱中迭代地发现和修复漏洞，确保代理在完成任务时不会被错误奖励。随着代理环境的数量和复杂性增加，修复可被利用的验证器变得尤为重要。我们的方法通过设置隔离的验证器沙箱和黑客修复循环，显著提高了对抗攻击的成功率。

papers.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
papers.abstract: Abstract PathFM is a trajectory-based forecasting model using flow matching to generate complete future paths, enabling efficient multi-path sampling and improved dependence modeling for time series.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.

ru.title: Прогнозируем не точки, а целые траектории будущего
ru.desc: В статье представлена модель PathFM для прогнозирования временных рядов, которая с помощью flow matching генерирует полные будущие траектории, а не только маргинальные квантили. Дистилляция сэмплера до одного-двух шагов и совместное использование кэша history attention позволяют получать несколько путей за время одного запроса к квантильной модели. Модель показывает конкурентную точность на fev-bench и TIME, а на новом бенчмарке fps-bench с energy и variogram score превосходит все внешние baseline. Эксперименты на хаотических системах demonstrate, что PathFM сохраняет долговременную вариативность, в то время как сильные baseline быстро схлопываются.

en.title: PathFM: Revolutionizing Time Series Forecasting with Complete Trajectory Generation
en.desc: PathFM is a novel forecasting model designed to predict future trajectories in time series data by utilizing flow matching techniques. Unlike traditional models that focus on predicting individual quantiles, PathFM generates complete future paths, capturing the dependence structure essential for applications like cumulative demand forecasting. The model is optimized for efficiency, allowing it to produce multiple paths in a timeframe comparable to querying a single quantile model. PathFM demonstrates superior performance on established benchmarks and introduces new evaluation metrics, making it a practical choice for generative time series forecasting.

zh.title: PathFM：高效的轨迹预测模型
zh.desc: PathFM是一种基于轨迹的预测模型，利用流匹配生成完整的未来路径，从而实现高效的多路径采样和改进的时间序列依赖建模。与传统模型主要预测边际分位数不同，PathFM能够更好地捕捉未来轨迹之间的依赖关系，这对于累积需求、峰值负载和事件时机等轨迹相关量至关重要。该模型通过历史注意力缓存和简化采样器，使得在一次查询量化模型所需的时间内生成多个路径成为可能。PathFM在多个预测基准测试中表现出色，尤其是在新的fps-bench评估中，展现了其在生成时间序列预测中的竞争力和实用性。

papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
papers.abstract: Abstract Personalizing sparse Mixture-of-Experts language models enables localized, interpretable control over user-specific behaviors through specialized expert routing and learned personalized latents.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.

ru.title: Персонализация LLM через локализованных экспертов: управляемость вместо черного ящика
ru.desc: Авторы предлагают персонализировать языковые модели типа Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), где каждый токен направляется маршрутизатором к небольшому числу специализированных экспертов. Такая разреженная архитектура снижает полисемантичность нейронов по сравнению с плотными LLM и позволяет локализовать компоненты, отвечающие за персонализацию. Для поиска интерпретируемых персонализированных латентных признаков обучаются crosscoders на парных активациях персонализированной и неперсонализированной моделей, после чего выделяются эксперты, кодирующие отдельные признаки персонализации. Эксперименты показывают, что персонализированные MoE-модели конкурентоспособны с плотными аналогами при активации лишь части параметров, а каузальные интервенции подтверждают, что усиление соответствующих экспертов переводит базовую модель к персонализированному поведению.

en.title: Personalized Control with Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Models
en.desc: This paper discusses a method for personalizing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models to improve user-specific interactions. By using specialized expert routing, the model reduces the complexity of polysemantic neurons, allowing for clearer understanding and control over personalized behaviors. The authors demonstrate that their personalized MoE models can achieve performance comparable to dense models while activating fewer parameters, leading to lower polysemanticity. Additionally, they show that the personalized latents can effectively capture distinct personalization features, enabling targeted adjustments to the model's behavior.

zh.title: 个性化混合专家模型：更少参数，更高控制
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种个性化稀疏混合专家语言模型的方法，以实现对用户特定行为的局部和可解释的控制。通过专门的专家路由和学习的个性化潜变量，减少了多义性，使得个性化的组件更易于理解和控制。我们在大规模个性化数据集上对三种开放权重的混合专家模型进行了适应，并训练了交叉编码器，以学习可解释的个性化潜变量。实验结果表明，个性化的混合专家模型在性能上与密集模型相当，同时激活的参数数量更少，且个性化潜变量与非个性化模型的共享程度较低。

papers.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
papers.abstract: Abstract H-DDCM replaces dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries and table-free lexicographic coding to enable scalable, efficient generative image and video compression using diffusion and flow models.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Training-free diffusion-based compression methods repurpose the generative priors of a diffusion or a flow model to compress data without retraining them as task-specific codecs. Recent codebook-based approaches such as Turbo-DDCM achieve strong perceptual quality at ultra-low bitrates, but their reliance on dense Gaussian codebooks remains costly in both memory and computation, and scales poorly with the large latent dimensions of modern image and video generators. Their combinatorial bitstream encoding further becomes computationally heavy at this scale. We introduce H-DDCM, a scalable generative compression framework that replaces Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries. The fast Walsh-Hadamard transform allows for implicitly synthesizing full-dimensional dictionaries with O(d log d) compute for projection and reconstruction and O(d) memory, without materializing the full-dimensional dictionary. We further introduce an efficient table-free lexicographic coding scheme that makes combinatorial encoding practical at larger dimensions. Beyond images, we adapt the framework to an autoregressive video flow model and develop a streaming compression scheme that periodically re-encodes recently reconstructed frames into a fresh KV-cache prefix, preserving temporal context across segments at no additional transmitted bits. This enables long-form, close to real-time generative video compression on a single GPU. Across image and video benchmarks, H-DDCM achieves competitive rate-distortion-perception performance while substantially reducing the memory and computational overhead of codebook-based training-free generative compression.

ru.title: Сжатие изображений и видео с помощью генеративных моделей — быстрее и легче
ru.desc: В статье представлен H-DDCM — масштабируемый фреймворк для генеративного сжатия изображений и видео без дообучения диффузионных и flow-моделей. Вместо плотных гауссовых кодбуков авторы используют неявные рандомизированные словари Адамара, которые вычисляются быстрым преобразованием Уолша–Адамара за O(d log d) с памятью O(d). Также предложено табличное-free лексикографическое кодирование, делающее комбинаторное кодирование практичным, и потоковая схема для видео с перекодированием кадров в новый префикс KV-кэша. Метод достигает конкурентного качества rate-distortion-perception при заметно меньших затратах памяти и вычислений.

en.title: Efficient Generative Compression with H-DDCM
en.desc: The paper introduces H-DDCM, a new framework for generative image and video compression that replaces traditional dense Gaussian codebooks with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries. This approach allows for efficient data compression using diffusion and flow models without the need for retraining, making it scalable and less resource-intensive. By utilizing the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform, H-DDCM achieves significant reductions in memory usage and computational costs while maintaining high perceptual quality. Additionally, the framework includes a novel table-free lexicographic coding scheme that enhances the practicality of encoding at larger dimensions, enabling effective long-form video compression.

zh.title: 高效生成压缩的新方法：H-DDCM
zh.desc: H-DDCM是一种新的生成压缩框架，它用隐式随机Hadamard字典替代了传统的密集高斯码本，从而实现了高效的图像和视频压缩。该方法利用快速的Walsh-Hadamard变换，能够在不实际生成完整字典的情况下，进行高效的投影和重建。H-DDCM还引入了一种无表的字典编码方案，使得在大维度下的组合编码变得可行。通过这种方法，H-DDCM在图像和视频基准测试中表现出竞争力的压缩性能，同时显著降低了内存和计算开销。

papers.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract SCOPED trains separate experts for distinct capabilities, extracts skills via reward-guided reflection, and distills procedural knowledge into a unified vision-language model without exposing explicit skills at inference, reducing cross-capability interference.  Generated by thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. This paper proposes Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation (SCOPED), which trains capability-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection. During on-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill-decoupled on-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student. All code and data are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/SCOPED.

ru.title: Развязываем навыки и объединяем экспертов в одну VLM без потери специализации
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод SCOPED, который обучает отдельных экспертов для разных визуальных способностей vision-language модели с помощью reinforcement learning. Навыки извлекаются через рефлексию, управляемую reward, и используются для on-policy дистилляции. Единая student-модель усваивает процедурные знания без явного доступа к навыкам на инференсе. Это снижает cross-capability interference и улучшает результаты на восьми мультимодальных бенчмарках.

en.title: Decoupling Skills for Enhanced Learning in Vision-Language Models
en.desc: The paper introduces SCOPED, a method that trains separate experts for different skills in vision-language models (VLMs) to avoid conflicts during training. By using reward-guided reflection, SCOPED extracts these skills without exposing them during inference, which helps the model learn procedural knowledge more effectively. This approach reduces interference from mixed objectives and enhances the model's ability to focus on relevant visual information. The results show that SCOPED outperforms traditional methods across multiple benchmarks, highlighting the benefits of skill-decoupled training in machine learning.

zh.title: 技能解耦，提升模型能力！
